setup.swiftui:
# Nucleux Mobile for SwiftUI

Requirements: iOS 17+, Swift tools 6.0 (Xcode 16 or later). The package is `Package.swift` at the repository root; sources in `swiftui/Sources/Nucleux`.

## 1. Add the package (SwiftPM, private repo)
Xcode → File → Add Package Dependencies → `https://github.com/intelligaia/nucleux-mobile.git` (you need read access), product **Nucleux**. Or in a Package.swift:
```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/intelligaia/nucleux-mobile.git", branch: "main"),
// target dependencies:
.product(name: "Nucleux", package: "nucleux-mobile"),
```
For a local checkout use `.package(path: "../nucleux-mobile")`.

## 2. Import
```swift
import Nucleux
```

## 3. Host every screen in NucleuxMenuHost
Menus (model menu, Add context, autocomplete, Request settings) are drawn by a host around the screen. Without it they never appear.
```swift
NucleuxMenuHost {
    YourScreen()
}
```

## Theming
Colours are `NucleuxColor.*` (`background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `mutedForeground`, `primary`, `info`, `brand`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`…). They are dynamic: they follow the system light/dark setting; force one with `.preferredColorScheme(.dark)`. Never hard-code colours.

## Fonts and icons
The Lucide icon font (`lucide.ttf`) is a package resource and registers itself the first time an icon is drawn (`NucleuxIconView(.sparkles)`). Nothing to add to Info.plist.

## Announcements and focus
Components announce state changes politely with `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(…).post()`; do the same for your own changes. Never move VoiceOver focus or raise the keyboard on your own.
setup.compose:
# Nucleux Mobile for Jetpack Compose

Requirements: minSdk 24, compileSdk 37, Kotlin 2.4.0, AGP 9.2.1, Compose BOM 2026.08.00, JVM toolchain 17. The library is the Gradle module `compose/nucleux` (namespace `com.intelligaia.nucleux`, explicit API); it is not published to a Maven repository yet.

## 1. Add the module (from a checkout of intelligaia/nucleux-mobile)
`settings.gradle.kts`:
```kotlin
include(":nucleux")
project(":nucleux").projectDir = file("../nucleux-mobile/compose/nucleux")
```
App `build.gradle.kts`:
```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation(project(":nucleux"))
}
```
The module uses the version catalog aliases in `compose/gradle/libs.versions.toml` (android-library, kotlin-compose, roborazzi plugins; compose-bom, compose-foundation, compose-ui, window); copy those entries into your catalog.

## 2. Import
```kotlin
import com.intelligaia.nucleux.*
import com.intelligaia.nucleux.icons.NucleuxIcons
```

## Theming
Wrap content in `NucleuxTheme { … }` (or `NucleuxTheme(darkTheme = true) { … }`) and read colours from `Nucleux.colors` (`background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `mutedForeground`, `info`, `brand`, `destructive`…). Without it, components follow the system light/dark setting. Never hard-code `Color(0xFF…)`.

## Fonts and icons
The Lucide font ships as `res/font/lucide.ttf` inside the module; draw icons with `NucleuxIcon(NucleuxIcons.Sparkles)`.

## Announcements and focus
Components announce state changes politely from the window (`View.announceForAccessibility`) and use polite live regions; do the same for your own changes. Never call `requestFocus()` on your own or raise the keyboard uninvited.
setup.flutter:
# Nucleux Mobile for Flutter

Requirements: Dart SDK ^3.9.0, Flutter >=3.35.0. The package is `flutter/` in the repository (name `nucleux`, not on pub.dev).

## 1. Add the dependency
`pubspec.yaml` (git, private repo):
```yaml
dependencies:
  nucleux:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/intelligaia/nucleux-mobile.git
      path: flutter
```
or a local checkout: `nucleux: { path: ../nucleux-mobile/flutter }`.

## 2. Import
```dart
import 'package:nucleux/nucleux.dart';
```

## Theming
`NucleuxTheme.of(context)` gives the colours (`background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `mutedForeground`, `info`, `brand`, `destructive`…) for the platform brightness; wrap with `NucleuxTheme(colors: NucleuxColors.dark, child: …)` to force one. Never hard-code `Color(0xFF…)` or `Colors.*`.

## Fonts and icons
The Lucide font is declared in the package's pubspec (family `lucide`); `NucleuxIcons.*` are `IconData` with `fontPackage: 'nucleux'`, so nothing is needed in your app's pubspec.

## Announcements and focus
Components announce politely with `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement`; do the same for your own changes. Never `requestFocus()` or `autofocus: true` on your own.
setup.react-native:
# Nucleux Mobile for React Native

Requirements: react >=19, react-native >=0.80. Package `@intelligaia/nucleux` (0.1.0), private, on GitHub Packages.

## 1. Install
(private, GitHub Packages)

```sh
# .npmrc in your app
@intelligaia:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
npm install @intelligaia/nucleux
```

## 2. Link the icon font
Icons are a subset of [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) shipped as `assets/fonts/lucide.ttf`. Apps must link it once.

React Native CLI: add to your app's `react-native.config.js`, then run `npx react-native-asset`:

```js
module.exports = { assets: ['./node_modules/@intelligaia/nucleux/assets/fonts'] };
```

Expo:

```js
import { useFonts } from 'expo-font';
const [loaded] = useFonts({ lucide: require('@intelligaia/nucleux/assets/fonts/lucide.ttf') });
```

## 3. Import
```tsx
import { PromptComposer, Caveat, NucleuxProvider } from '@intelligaia/nucleux';
```

## Theming
Components follow the system light/dark setting; force one with `<NucleuxProvider scheme="dark">…</NucleuxProvider>`. Read colours with `const c = useNucleuxColors()` (`c.background`, `c.foreground`, `c.mutedForeground`, `c.info`, `c.brand`, `c.destructive`…). Never hard-code `'#…'` or `rgb(…)`.

## Announcements and focus
Components announce politely with `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility`; do the same for your own changes. Never `autoFocus` or `.focus()` a field on your own.

components.specText:
# Button

Web source of truth: `@nucleux/button` (`packages/button/src/index.tsx` in intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux).

| Platform | Name | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxButton` | ✅ reference |
| Compose | `NucleuxButton` | ✅ reference |
| Flutter | `NucleuxButton` | ✅ reference |
| React Native | `Button` from `@intelligaia/nucleux` | ✅ reference |

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Web equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | text | required | `children` |
| variant | `primary` · `cta` · `secondary` · `ghost` · `destructive` | `primary` | `variant` |
| size | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | `md` | `size` (`icon` comes with IconButton) |
| leadingIcon / trailingIcon | platform icon | none | `leftIcon` / `rightIcon` |
| enabled | bool | true | `disabled` (inverted) |
| onPress | callback | required | `onClick` |

## Visuals (match web)

| Variant | Background | Content | Border | Shadow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary | `primary` | `primaryForeground` | `border` | small |
| cta | `info` | `infoForeground` | `border` | small |
| secondary | `background` | `foreground` | `border` | small |
| ghost | none | `foreground` | none | none |
| destructive | `destructive` | `destructiveForeground` | `border` | small |

| Size | Visual height | Horizontal padding | Font |
|---|---|---|---|
| sm | 32 | 12 | 14 semibold |
| md | 36 | 16 | 14 semibold |
| lg | 40 | 20 | 14 semibold |

- Corner radius `radius.lg` (12). Icon–label gap 6.
- Pressed: background at 90% opacity (web hover). Ghost pressed: `accent` background.
- Disabled: whole button at 50% opacity, not tappable.

## Mobile rules (beyond web)

- **Tap target ≥ 44pt (iOS) / 48dp (Android)** whatever the visual height. The extra area is invisible.
- Font scales with Dynamic Type / Android font scale; height grows with it (min height, not fixed height).
- Label never truncates silently: it wraps up to 2 lines at large text sizes.
- Accessibility: role button, label = text, disabled state announced.
- Works in light and dark mode through the color tokens; no hardcoded colors.

## Open design questions

- Mobile platforms usually use 44–48pt-tall buttons. Should `md` stay 36 (web parity) or become 44 on mobile? Currently web parity plus an enlarged tap area.

components.specText:
# IconButton

Web source of truth: `@nucleux/icon-button` (`packages/icon-button/src/index.tsx` in intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux).
Used by Initial CTA for Add context (+), voice and send.

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxIconButton` |
| Compose | `NucleuxIconButton` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxIconButton` |
| React Native | `IconButton` from `@intelligaia/nucleux` |

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Web equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| icon | platform icon (tinted by the button) | required | `children` |
| label | text, announced by screen readers | **required** | `aria-label` (required) |
| variant | `ghost` · `active` · `solid` | `ghost` | `variant` |
| size | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | `md` | `size` |
| enabled | bool | true | `disabled` (inverted) |
| onPress | callback | required | `onClick` |

The icon is supplied by the caller (SF Symbol, vector, any widget). Nucleux doesn't ship an icon set yet; that decision comes with PromptComposer.

## Visuals (match web)

| Variant | Background | Icon color | Corner radius | Shadow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ghost | none | `mutedForeground` | `radius.md` (10) | none |
| active | `accent` | `foreground` | `radius.md` (10) | none |
| solid | `primary` | `primaryForeground` | `radius.lg` (12) | small |

| Size | Visual box |
|---|---|
| sm | 32 × 32 |
| md | 36 × 36 |
| lg | 40 × 40 |

- Icon 20 × 20, centred.
- Pressed: ghost takes the `accent` background and `foreground` icon (web hover); solid goes to 90% opacity; active doesn't change.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not tappable.

## Mobile rules (beyond web)

- **Tap target** is square and at least 44pt (iOS) / 48dp (Android). On iOS it grows to 48pt when the person uses large text (text scale ≥ 1.3), per the Initial CTA parity table ("44px, 48 with large text").
- Screen readers announce the label and the button role; there is no visible text, so a missing label is a bug. Each platform enforces this at compile time where it can (required parameter).
- The icon doesn't scale with text size: it is a fixed 20 × 20 inside a box that only grows in tap area.

## Not in scope

- Send's empty / typing / ready states are composer logic (see PromptComposer), built from `solid` disabled, `active` and `solid`.
- Keyboard shortcut hints (`aria-keyshortcuts`) don't apply on touch screens; the parity table says the send-key hint is hidden on every touch screen.

components.specText:
# ModelChip

The resting control of the **Model Selection** pattern (pattern library, branch-2, `material-patterns.js` → `model-selection`), as it sits in the composer of **Initial CTA**. The menu it opens (model list, then effort) is a separate component, built later.

There is no web-kit component for this; the source is the pattern library's markup and CSS (`.ax__mode--model`). Visuals use Nucleux tokens; the pattern library's Material styling is not copied (see Open questions in the build log).

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxModelChip` |
| Compose | `NucleuxModelChip` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxModelChip` |
| React Native | `ModelChip` from `@intelligaia/nucleux` |

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| model | text | required | e.g. "Balanced". Long names are normal (a real identifier easily passes 25 characters) |
| effort | text or none | none | e.g. "High" |
| effortDescription | text or none | none | e.g. "Works through it step by step". Spoken only |
| showsEffort | bool | true | The composer sets false at window width ≤ 390pt: the chip shows the model only; effort stays in the menu and in the spoken label |
| expanded | bool | false | True while its menu is open |
| enabled | bool | true | |
| onPress | callback | required | Opens the menu |

## Visuals

| Part | Style |
|---|---|
| Container | Transparent. Pressed or expanded: `accent` background. Corner `radius.md` (10). Horizontal padding 12. Height at least 44 |
| Model | 14pt semibold, `foreground`. One line, cut off with "…" when too long |
| Effort | 14pt regular, `foreground`, 6pt after the model. Never cut off: the model gives up room first |

The pattern's rule: the chip "truncates before anything wraps". The full name is always in the spoken label and one tap away in the menu.

## Large text

When text is scaled to 1.3× or more (pattern: `data-text="large"`):

- Nothing is cut off: model and effort wrap onto more lines.
- Height at least 48.
- The effort shows even if `showsEffort` is false.
- Placement on its own row is the composer's job.

## Accessibility

- Role: button that opens a menu. Expanded or collapsed state announced where the platform supports it (Compose, Flutter, React Native; iOS has no expanded state, so it uses the hint).
- Label: "Model: Balanced. Effort: High — Works through it step by step. Change them." Without effort: "Model: Balanced. Change it."
- Hint (iOS) / description: "Opens the model menu."
- The visible text is not read separately.

## Not in scope

- The menu (Auto switch, model rows with "what it's for", unavailable and restricted rows, effort slider) → ModelMenu, later.
- "Using X from your next message" status and the withdrawn-model alert → ModelMenu.
- Hiding effort at ≤ 390pt and taking its own row at large text → PromptComposer decides; the chip only follows `showsEffort` and its own large-text rules.

components.specText:
# PromptComposer

The shared composer from the pattern library (branch-2, `material-patterns.js` → `initial-cta` and `open-input`; CSS `.ax__composer`). One component: Initial CTA uses it on an empty workspace, then the same composer docks under the conversation. Its parts are already built: IconButton (Add context, voice, send), ModelChip, Lucide icons.

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxPromptComposer` |
| Compose | `NucleuxPromptComposer` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxPromptComposer` |
| React Native | `PromptComposer` from `@intelligaia/nucleux` |

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| text | text, two-way | required | The host owns it (and clears it after a send) |
| label | text | required | Accessible name, e.g. "Start a task with Aria". Never the placeholder |
| placeholder | text | none | An active suggestion: "What would you like to work on?" |
| model, effort, effortDescription | text | none | Shown in a ModelChip when `model` is set |
| modelMenuExpanded | bool | false | Passed to the chip |
| onModelPress | callback | none | |
| onAddContext | callback | none | Add context (+) is hidden when not given |
| onVoice | callback | none | Voice is hidden when not given |
| onSend | callback(text) | required | Receives the text as typed |
| maxLines | number | 8 | Growth ceiling; then the field scrolls. 1 keeps it to one line (and never expands) |
| readyDelay | ms | 600 | How long a pause makes Send "ready" |

## Send states

| State | When | Send button |
|---|---|---|
| Empty | No text, or only spaces and line breaks | IconButton `solid`, disabled |
| Typing | Text changed less than `readyDelay` ago | IconButton `active` (secondary emphasis) |
| Ready | Text present and no change for `readyDelay` | IconButton `solid` |

A pause never sends. Only tapping Send calls `onSend`. The two enabled states differ in fill and in emphasis, not color alone. Send's spoken label is "Send".

## Layout

The composer measures its own width, so a split screen or one pane of a folded device behaves like a phone.

| Condition | Layout |
|---|---|
| Width under 600 (a phone, one pane of a fold) | **Stacked**: the field on its own line, then the controls: + on the left, the model chip next to it (giving way first), then voice and send on the right. Field starts 2 lines tall |
| Width 600 or more (open iPhone Duo, unfolded Fold, tablet) | **Row**: + · field · chip · voice · send on one line. Field starts 1 line tall |
| Large text (1.3× or more), any width | Field on its own line, the model chip on its own full-width line, then + · voice · send. Buttons grow to 48 |
| Width under 370 | The chip hides the effort (a 390pt screen minus 16pt side margins). The effort stays in the chip's spoken label |

- Field text is 16pt (mobile: stops iOS zooming and reads comfortably), scaled with the text-size setting.
- The field grows a line at a time up to `maxLines` (eight unless the host says otherwise), then scrolls inside.
- Controls sit on the bottom line when the field wraps (row layout).

## Expand and Collapse

The library's composer height rule (21 Oct 2026, `material-sim.js`, "THE COMPOSER'S HEIGHT"), as ChatGPT and other agentic tools do it. The rules live in `react-native/src/composerHeight.ts`; `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/composer-height.fixtures.json`.

- **Expand** appears in the composer's top-right corner once the request needs more lines than the cap: a 32 icon button (`maximize-2`, `mutedForeground`) in a 44 / 48 target, the field keeping room beside it. Spoken "Expand the composer".
- **Expanded**, the field takes the composer's full width above the controls (in the row layout too) and most of the height there is: at least two lines more than the cap, otherwise 62% of the window up to 640, and never so tall that the composer's controls leave what the screen shows (64 kept above it, with the keyboard and safe areas taken out). The control becomes **Collapse** (`minimize-2`, "Collapse the composer").
- **Collapse**, or sending (which empties the field), brings back the eight-line field. An empty field is never expanded.
- **No Expand** on a one-line field (`maxLines` 1) or in voice mode.
- Pressing it keeps the keyboard as it was: if the field had focus it keeps it.

| | Text | Read aloud |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed | none (icon) | "Expand the composer" |
| Expanded | none (icon) | "Collapse the composer" |

Ours, not the library's: the icon (Lucide's nearest to Material `open_in_full` / `close_fullscreen`); "what the screen shows" for the library's "the surface that holds it" (on a phone, the keyboard takes most of it); focus only comes back to the field if it was there (the library always focuses it, which would raise the keyboard).

## Visuals

| Part | Style |
|---|---|
| Container | `background`, 1pt `border` outline, corner 24, padding 8, subtle shadow |
| Focused | Outline turns `primary` and the corner squares up to 20: a shape change as well as a color change |
| Placeholder | `mutedForeground`, one line, cut off with "…" (the field still grows for real text) |
| Field text | 16pt `foreground` |

## Accessibility

- The field's accessible name is `label`; the placeholder is a suggestion only.
- Every control is at least 44pt / 48dp (inherited from IconButton and ModelChip).
- Focus is shown by color and shape.

## Not in scope (later)

- Hand-over to the docked composer and its animation → Initial CTA.
- Keyboard avoidance → the screen that hosts the composer (Initial CTA).
- Voice mode inside the composer, attachments row, send errors, the Add context menu → later components.
- Hardware-keyboard Return to send: on touch keyboards Return adds a line; there is no key hint on touch screens.

components.specText:
# Initial CTA

The pattern library's Initial CTA (branch-2, `material-patterns.js` → `initial-cta`; mobile parity table in `mobile-patterns.js`). The empty workspace: one PromptComposer as the only focal point, with an optional supporting line. After the first send, the same composer docks at the bottom and the conversation takes the space.

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxInitialCTA` |
| Compose | `NucleuxInitialCta` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxInitialCta` |
| React Native | `InitialCta` from `@intelligaia/nucleux` |

## API

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| started | bool | False: the invitation. True: the conversation is shown and the composer is docked |
| supportingText | text or none | One short line: where this is and what the agent can reach. Never a headline |
| fold | Fold or none | `{ axis: vertical \| horizontal, position, size }` in the container's coordinates. Android and Flutter read it from the system; SwiftUI and React Native take it from the host for now |
| composer | the PromptComposer | The host passes its composer; it is never rebuilt, so typed text and focus survive the hand-over |
| conversation | content | Shown once `started` |

## Geometry

One pure function decides where everything goes: `initialCtaLayout(width, height, fold, started, composerHeight, leadHeight)`. The TypeScript version (`react-native/src/initialCtaLayout.ts`) is the reference. `npm run fixtures` runs it over every device pose from `mobile-patterns.js` and writes `specs/initial-cta.fixtures.json`; the SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter versions are tested against that file, so all four lay out identically.

| Arrangement | When | Composer | Supporting line |
|---|---|---|---|
| compact | No fold, container under 420 | Full width less 16 margins, anchored at the bottom (by the thumb and the keyboard) | Left-aligned, 14pt, 14 above the composer |
| centered | No fold, 420 and wider | Up to 720 wide, centred; line and composer centred as a group | Centred, 15pt, up to 400 wide |
| splitVertical | A vertical fold (iPhone Duo book, Galaxy Fold unfolded) | In the trailing pane, at the bottom | In the leading pane, 17pt, up to 300 wide, bottom-aligned |
| splitHorizontal | A horizontal fold (tabletop) | Below the fold: centred in the lower half; docked at the bottom once started | Above the fold, centred, 16 above it |
| working | Started, no fold | Docked at the bottom, centred, up to 720 | Hidden |

- The gutter over a fold is the fold's width, but never less than 24. Nothing is placed on it.
- Once started, the conversation fills the space above the composer (in the trailing pane on a vertical fold, above the fold on a horizontal one).
- Composer width 720 means open iPhone Duo and tabletop get the one-row composer; phones and single panes get the stacked one.

## Motion

- Hand-over on first send: the composer moves to its docked place over **500ms** on the emphasized curve `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`, no overshoot. The supporting line fades.
- Reduced motion: no movement; the composer is simply in its new place.

## Keyboard

The layout works in the area left above the keyboard: the composer is anchored to the bottom, so the empty space gives way first and the composer rides above the keyboard.

## Accessibility

- The region is named "New conversation".
- On hand-over, "Conversation started" is announced politely; focus stays in the composer's field.
- The supporting line is plain text, read before the composer.

inCases: iPhone 18 Pro, initial, no supporting line
iPhone Duo closed, initial, no supporting line
iPhone Duo open, initial, no supporting line
iPhone Duo book, initial, no supporting line
Galaxy Fold folded, initial, no supporting line
Galaxy Fold unfolded, initial, no supporting line
Galaxy Fold tabletop, initial, no supporting line
Small phone, initial, no supporting line

components.specText:
# ModelMenu

The menu ModelChip opens, from the pattern library's **Model Selection** pattern (branch-2, `material-patterns.js` → `model-selection`; CSS `.md-ml`, `.md-mle`). Two screens in one panel: the model list, then that model's effort. Visuals use Nucleux tokens.

This component is the **panel** (content, screens, states). Presenting it as a flyout anchored above the chip is a separate, shared component (the Menu surface), also used by the Add context menu.

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxModelMenu` |
| Compose | `NucleuxModelMenu` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxModelMenu` |
| React Native | `ModelMenu` from `@intelligaia/nucleux` |

## Data

| Type | Fields |
|---|---|
| ModelOption | `id`, `name`, `purpose` (one line saying what it is **for**, never a spec sheet), `availability`, optional `meta` (at most one attribute, e.g. "Uses more allowance") |
| Availability | `available` · `unavailable(note)` (temporarily down; note says what to use meanwhile) · `restricted(note)` (an organization decided; note says who decides) |
| EffortLevel | `id`, `name` ("High"), `description` ("Works through it step by step"). Ordinal: 3 or 5 levels |

## API

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| models | ModelOption[] | In display order. The host may leave restricted models out ("restriction as absence") and set `restrictedNote` |
| selectedModelId | id | |
| auto | `{ on, description }` or none | The Auto switch. Description says what it weighs: "Appropriate model for each request, balancing quality and speed." |
| efforts | EffortLevel[] | |
| selectedEffortId | id | |
| restrictedNote | text or none | One line under the list explaining a shortened list |
| onSelectModel(id), onAutoChange(on), onSelectEffort(id) | callbacks | The host updates its state; the chip's new label is the confirmation |

## Screens

**1. Models**

- Heading "MODELS" (small, uppercase, muted).
- **Auto** switch row at the top: name, description (always shown, on or off), switch. Turning it on collapses the model rows and moves on to the effort screen.
- A divider, then one row per model (hidden while Auto is on):
  - Leading 24pt tick column: a check on the selected row.
  - Name (14 semibold), then a tag when blocked: "Temporarily unavailable" (neutral fill) or "Restricted" (outline only).
  - Purpose (13, muted). For blocked rows, the note on its own line (12).
  - Trailing chevron on available rows only: it says "pressing moves on to effort".
  - Selected row: `accent` background **and** the tick (never color alone).
  - Blocked rows: disabled but readable (name and purpose at 70%); restricted rows also get a faint fill.
  - At least 48 tall.
- `restrictedNote` under the list, if given.
- Tapping an available row selects it (`onSelectModel`) and replaces the list with its effort screen.

**2. Effort**

- Breadcrumb button: back chevron, the model name, the effort value in `primary`. Goes back to the list.
- The effort slider: one track with a notch per level and one handle. Tap a notch or drag; the value snaps to levels. Filled to the handle in `primary`.
- Spoken value: "High — Works through it step by step". Adjustable with swipe up/down (VoiceOver, TalkBack) and arrow keys.

## Size

- Width: 300 to 340, never wider than the window minus 32.
- Height: up to 58% of the window or 430, whichever is smaller; the list scrolls inside.

## Accessibility

- Model rows are radio items reporting selected / not selected; blocked rows are disabled but still read their note.
- Auto is a switch with its description.
- The breadcrumb's label: "Back to models. Balanced, High".
- The slider is one adjustable control with a spoken value; the notches themselves are not separate stops.

## Also provided

- `modelChangeNote(name)` → "Using Deep reasoning from your next message": the one line the host shows under the composer after a change (polite live region). No toast.

## Not in scope (later)

- Presenting the panel (the shared Menu surface).
- The "model withdrawn" fallback alert.
- Grouping by provider; ModelCredit on answers.

components.specText:
# Menu surface

The flyout that presents a Nucleux menu next to the control that opened it: the model menu from the model chip, the Add context menu from +. From the pattern library's shared menu surface (`.ax__menu` in `material-pattern.html`): anchored to its control, opening upward from the composer.

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `.nucleuxMenu(isPresented:align:fold:content:)` on the anchor, inside a `NucleuxMenuHost` |
| Compose | `NucleuxMenuSurface(expanded, onDismiss, anchor bounds…)` built on `Popup` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxMenuAnchor` built on `OverlayPortal` |
| React Native | `MenuSurface` built on `Modal` |

## Placement

One pure function, `menuPlacement(window, insets, anchor, menu size, align, matchRect, fold)`. The TypeScript version (`react-native/src/menuPlacement.ts`) is the reference; `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/menu-placement.fixtures.json` (12 cases on iPhone, iPhone Duo and Galaxy Fold), and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

- **Direction:** opens **upward**, 10 above the anchor. If it doesn't fit above but fits below, it opens downward. If it fits neither, it takes the larger side and is shortened; its content scrolls.
- **Alignment:** `start` (menu's leading edge on the anchor's), `end` (trailing edges), or `match` (the x and width of a given rectangle: the Add context menu takes the composer's width).
- **Margins:** at least 16 from the window edges and inside the safe area (status bar, home indicator).
- **Folds:** the menu stays in the anchor's own pane (vertical fold) or half (horizontal fold), at least 12 from the fold. Nothing sits on a fold.

## Surface

| Part | Style |
|---|---|
| Container | `background`, corner 16, 1pt `border`, soft shadow |
| Content | The panel (ModelMenu, Add context menu); it scrolls if the surface was shortened |
| Open / close | Fade and slight scale from the anchor's side, 200ms on the emphasized curve. None under reduced motion |

## Behavior

- Tap outside, Android back, or the hardware Escape key closes it. Tapping the anchor again also closes it (the outside tap lands first).
- The prompt text and the composer are untouched while it is open.

## Accessibility

- When it opens, screen-reader focus moves into the menu; when it closes, focus returns to the anchor.
- The surface is modal for screen readers (content behind is not reachable while it's open) and has a two-finger scrub / escape action to close.
- The anchor reports expanded / collapsed (ModelChip already does).

inCases: phone, model menu from the chip (composer low)
phone, model menu from a chip near the top: opens down
phone, model menu from mid-screen: neither side fits, larger side, shortened
iPhone Duo closed, model menu wider than the window allows
iPhone Duo closed, chip near the right edge
iPhone Duo open, model menu aligned to the chip end
iPhone Duo open, Add context from + (centred composer)
Galaxy Fold tabletop, no fold given: crosses the middle
Galaxy Fold tabletop, stays below the fold, shortened
iPhone Duo book, model menu stays in the right pane
iPhone Duo book, chip in the right pane near the fold

components.specText:
# AddContextMenu

The menu the composer's **+** opens (pattern library, branch-2: `.ax__menu--plus` and `.ax__mitem` in `material-pattern.html`; items from `material-sim.js`; mobile parity row "Add context (+)" in `mobile-patterns.js`). Presented with the Menu surface at the **composer's width**, opening upward from +.

| Platform | Name |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxAddContextMenu`; composer `addContextItems:` |
| Compose | `NucleuxAddContextMenu`; composer `addContextItems =` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxAddContextMenu`; composer `addContextItems:` |
| React Native | `AddContextMenu`; composer `addContextItems` |

## Items

The host decides what is on it; the pattern's products use two or three plain labels:

> Attach a file · Add a source · Add context — Upload image · Take photo · Share screen — Add images or files · Use connectors ›

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | Returned on selection |
| `label` | A verb phrase. No icon is required (the pattern has none); an optional bundled icon may lead |
| `hasSubmenu` | The row opens a second level: it shows a chevron and reports "has popup" |

## Rows

- At least **48** tall (parity table: "menu opens upward at the composer's width with 48px rows").
- Label 14 `foreground`; optional 20 icon `mutedForeground`; 11 horizontal padding; corner `radius.sm`; pressed: `accent` background.
- A submenu row adds a trailing chevron and stays highlighted while its level is open.

## Behavior

- Tapping a plain row calls `onSelect(id)` and closes the menu.
- Tapping a submenu row **drills in**: the list is replaced by that row's submenu (supplied by the host), headed by a "‹ {label}" back row. On desktop the pattern opens the second level beside its row; a phone has no room for that.
- The menu is presented by the composer: + toggles it; it takes the composer's x and width (Menu surface `match` alignment) and opens upward.

## Accessibility

- Rows are menu items; a submenu row reports that it opens a menu, and whether it is open.
- The surface is named "Add context".
- The + button reports expanded while the menu is open.

components.specText:
# Attachments

The pattern library's **Attachments** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `attachments`; `material-attach.js` for states and copy; CSS `.ax__atts`, `.md-att`). What appears in the composer after "Attach a file": one chip per file, on its own row above the field, inside the composer.

| Platform | Names |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxAttachment`, `NucleuxAttachmentChip`, `NucleuxAttachmentRow`; composer `attachments:` |
| Compose | same names; composer `attachments =` |
| Flutter | same names; composer `attachments:` |
| React Native | `Attachment`, `AttachmentChip`, `AttachmentRow`; composer `attachments` |

## Data

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id`, `name` | |
| `kind` | `document` · `spreadsheet` · `image` |
| `type`, `size` | "PDF · 34 pages", "2.4 MB": what predicts whether the agent can read it |
| `state` | below |
| `progress` | 0–100 while uploading, when there is a real number |
| `note` | The reason, for problem states ("Too large — 500 MB is the limit"); replaces type and size |
| `thumbnail` | Images only. Documents never get a preview: an invented page is a claim about content nobody has read |

## States

| State | Word | Bar | Look | Busy / stop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| queued | Waiting to upload | indeterminate | muted | busy |
| uploading | Uploading | **determinate** (`progress`), or indeterminate without a number | muted | busy |
| processing | Reading | **indeterminate**: uploaded is not readable | muted | busy |
| ready | Ready | none | word in `primary` | |
| partial | Partly read | none | word in `foreground` | |
| tooLarge | Too large | none | `destructive` edge, faint `destructive` fill, word in `destructive` | stop |
| unsupported | Not supported | none | same | stop |
| failed | Upload failed | none | same, **plus Retry** | stop |

- The state is always written first in the meta line, then "· type · size" (or the note instead).
- Never "Ready" while the file is still being read.
- Under reduced motion the indeterminate bar is a static half-width track; the word carries the state.

## Chip

- Lead: a 24 rounded box with the kind's icon (`file-text`, `file-spreadsheet`, `image`), or the image's thumbnail.
- Name 13 `foreground`, one line, cut off with "…". Meta 11 `mutedForeground`, one line.
- Progress: a 2pt hairline along the bottom edge, just inside the border.
- Buttons: Retry (failed only), Remove (always). 24 visual, 44 tap area. Labels name the file: "Try Northwind-proposal.pdf again", "Remove Northwind-proposal.pdf".
- Border `border`, background `background`, corner `radius.lg`, at least 48 tall.

## Row

- Chips wrap within the row; each keeps its own state.
- Past three rows the row scrolls (162: three 48 chips and their gaps; the pattern's 132 was for 40px desktop chips), so a tenth file can't push the field off the screen.
- Named "Attached to this message" and announces a summary politely as states change:
  "1 file attached and ready" · "3 files attached, 1 still being read" · "2 files attached, 1 could not be used" · "Nothing attached".

## In the composer

- `attachments` + `onRemoveAttachment(id)` + `onRetryAttachment(id)`.
- The row sits inside the composer, above the field.
- While anything is attached, one sentence sits under the composer: "Attached files stay with this conversation. Removing one takes it out of what comes next; it cannot unwrite an answer it has already shaped."
- Send stays as before; the host decides whether to wait for busy files.

## Helpers

- `attachmentsSummary(list)` → the live-region sentence.
- `attachmentTooLargeNote("500 MB")` → "Too large — 500 MB is the limit".
- `ATTACHMENT_LIFETIME` → the lifetime sentence.

Read as text only past page 100

components.specText:
# Voice input

The pattern library's **Voice Input** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `voice-input`; the session in `material-sim.js` (`vx*` functions); the indicator in `material-voice.js`; CSS `.ax__composer[data-mode="voice"]`, `.md-vx__panel`, `.ax__vxfrom`). Voice is a **mode of the same composer**, never a separate screen or composer: speak, see the words, correct them, send them yourself.

## What Nucleux provides, and what the app provides

| Nucleux | The app |
|---|---|
| The voice session: states, transitions, every word on screen and every announcement (`voiceReduce`) | Real speech recognition (Speech framework, SpeechRecognizer, a plugin…) |
| The composer's voice mode, the panels, the From-voice marker, the activity indicator | The OS microphone permission prompt, after the person presses "Allow microphone" |
| A clock (one tick a second) | Feeding heard words, the audio level, and the final result into the session |

## The session (one pure function)

`voiceReduce(session, event) → { session, announcement }`. The TypeScript version (`react-native/src/voiceSession.ts`) is the reference; `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/voice.fixtures.json` (event sequences and what they must produce), and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

| State | Bar | Panel above the bar | Announced (politely) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ready | Ordinary composer; mic "Speak instead of typing" | | |
| permission | Ordinary composer | "Use your microphone?" + what, why, when on, how to stop · **Not now** · **Allow microphone** | "Microphone access needed." |
| listening | Voice mode: indicator, "Listening · 0:04", typed words then heard words · **Pause** · **Stop** · **Cancel** | | "Microphone on. Listening." |
| paused | "Paused · microphone off · 0:04"; words kept · **Resume** · **Stop** · **Cancel** | | "Paused. The microphone is off; what you said is kept." |
| processing | "Transcribing…" · **Cancel** only | | "Microphone off. Transcribing." |
| transcribed | Ordinary composer, the words in the field; marker "From voice — check it before you send" · **Undo** | | "Transcribed into the message. Check it, edit it, then send when ready. Nothing was sent." |
| editing | Same; marker "From voice · edited — check it before you send" | | |
| couldn't understand | Ordinary composer, field unchanged | "Couldn't make out all of that." + "We kept what we heard: “…”" · **Type instead** · **Edit captured text** · **Retry** | the failure + "Retry, edit what was captured, or type instead." |
| denied | Ordinary composer | | "Microphone not allowed. Keep typing." |
| unavailable | Mic "Voice input unavailable", disabled | "Voice isn't available right now" + reason · **Type instead** | "Voice input is unavailable. Type instead." (on press) |

Rules from the pattern:

- **Stop never sends.** It keeps the words for review.
- **Cancel discards only the recording**; typed text stays.
- **Nothing is guessed**: under 3 words, or a failed result, is "couldn't understand", with what was heard kept.
- Joining: heard words are added after the typed text; capitalized when they start a sentence; a full stop added if missing.
- 60 second limit: "Time limit reached." then it stops (still never sends).
- Undo returns to exactly what was typed before.

## Controls (labels say what happens to the words)

| Control | Spoken label |
|---|---|
| Pause | "Pause — the microphone turns off, what you said is kept" |
| Resume | "Resume listening" |
| Stop | "Stop and keep what you said" |
| Cancel | "Cancel — discard this recording, your typed text stays" ("Cancel — discard this recording" while transcribing) |
| Undo (marker) | "Undo the transcript, back to what you had typed" |

All at least 48 on phones; the voice bar never wraps into two rows.

## Look

- Voice mode: the composer's outline turns `primary` at 55%; minimum height 64.
- Activity indicator: five short capsules whose length follows the real audio level (smoothed); a row of dots in silence; a slow low swell while transcribing. Hidden from screen readers (the status words say it). **Under reduced motion it is pinned**; the words carry the state.
- Status 13 `foreground`; heard line 12 `mutedForeground`, one line, cut off.
- Panels sit above the composer, never over it: title 14 semibold with an icon, text 13, actions as small Buttons. The couldn't-understand panel has a `destructive` icon, not a red flood.
- Marker: 16 mic icon in `primary`, 12 text, Undo as a ghost Button.

## Not in scope (later)

- The soft gradient behind the bar.
- Hands-free auto-stop after silence (the reducer supports a `silence` event; off by default).

components.specText:
# Open Input

The pattern library's **Open Input** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `open-input`; the simulator in `material-sim.js`; CSS `.ax__composer[data-error]`, `.ax__err`, `.ax__cbtn--stop`, `.md-oi`). It is **not a second component**: it is the shared PromptComposer at its working size, docked under the conversation, persistent after every send. Initial CTA is the same composer at its larger size.

What the pattern adds to the composer:

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| running | bool | false | The agent is answering. The send slot is **Stop**; the field stays live for the next request |
| onStop | callback | none | Withdraws the request |
| sendError | `send` · `offline` · `unavailable` · none | none | The last send didn't happen. The text is kept |
| onRetry | callback(text) | none | Sends the request **as it now is**, after any edits |
| agentName | text | "The assistant" | For "Aria is temporarily unavailable…" and the working note |
| sendKey | `enter` · `mod` | `enter` | Hardware keyboards only. Touch keyboards: Return always adds a line |
| appearance | `outlined` · `tonal` | `outlined` | Tonal: a filled container, no outline, for hosts whose surfaces are already outlined. Focus and error still draw their edges |
| density | `regular` · `compact` | `regular` | Compact: less padding (5/6, min height 52). Tap targets unchanged |

## Shared rules

`react-native/src/openInput.ts` is the reference; `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/open-input.fixtures.json` and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

**The send slot** (`sendSlot(entry, running, error)`):

| Situation | Button | Enabled |
|---|---|---|
| running | Stop (square icon, solid) | yes |
| sendError `offline` or `unavailable` | Send, **held** | no, until Retry |
| sendError `send` | Send as usual | yes when there's text |
| otherwise | Send: empty, typing (secondary), ready (primary) | when there's text |

**Failures, in words** (never a code):

| Kind | Row | Announced (alert) |
|---|---|---|
| send | "Couldn’t send your request. It’s still here — edit it or try again." | "Couldn’t send your request. It is still in the field." |
| offline | "You’re offline. Your request is kept — send it when you’re back online." | "You’re offline. Your request is kept." |
| unavailable | "Aria is temporarily unavailable. Your request is kept — try again in a moment." | "Aria is temporarily unavailable. Your request is kept." |

(The offline wording is ours: the pattern names the case but gives no sentence.)

**Send key** (`sendKeyAction`): `enter`: Return sends, Shift+Return adds a line. `mod`: ⌘/Ctrl+Return sends, Return adds a line. No hint line is printed; the send button carries the shortcut where the platform can show it (iPad's ⌘ overlay).

**Stop** (`stopRestore`): the withdrawn request comes back into the field, unless the person has already started typing the next one.

**Announcements:** "Sent. The composer is empty and ready for the next request." when `running` starts; "Stopped. Your request is back in the field." on Stop.

**Working note** under the composer while running: "Aria is working. Keep writing — Stop withdraws the request and gives it back."

## The composer does, the host does

| Composer | Host |
|---|---|
| Remembers what it last sent, and puts it back on Stop | Clears the text **only after a send succeeds** |
| Shows the error row, marks the field invalid, announces | Sets `sendError` when a send fails; clears it on success |
| Holds Send for offline / unavailable | Calls the agent; sets `running` |
| Returns focus to the field (caret at the end) after a menu closes or voice ends, when the field had it before | |

## Look

- Error: the outline takes `destructive`; a row inside the composer, above the untouched text: circle-alert icon 18 in `destructive`, the sentence 13 `foreground`, Retry as a small ghost Button; background `destructive` at 10%, corner 12, padding 4/4/4/12.
- The row and growth just appear under reduced motion.
- Stop: the solid icon button with the square icon.
- Tonal: `muted` fill, no outline or shadow until focus or error.

## Accessibility

- The field keeps its own name; with an error it is marked invalid and its hint is the error sentence.
- The error row is an alert; Retry is a button reachable right after it.
- Stop's spoken label is "Stop"; Send reports disabled while held.

## Not in scope (later)

- Hardware send key in React Native: `TextInput` can't tell a hardware Return or its modifiers from the touch keyboard's. Return always adds a line there.
- The conversation thread itself (host).

components.specText:
# Suggested Prompts

The pattern library's **Suggested Prompts** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `suggested-prompts`; the simulator and `suggestions()` renderer in `material-sim.js`; CSS `.md-sp`). Three or four ready-made requests, drawn from what the workspace shows, sit directly under the composer before the conversation starts. Choosing one **places** its fuller prompt in the composer's field as ordinary, editable text. Nothing is sent.

It is a composer option, like attachments: the suggestions only ever put words in the composer's field, so the composer places them, moves focus and announces.

| Platform | Names |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxSuggestedPrompt`; `.nucleuxSuggestions(_:label:started:after:layout:)` on the composer |
| Compose | `NucleuxSuggestedPrompt`; composer `suggestions = NucleuxSuggestions(...)` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxSuggestedPrompt`; composer `suggestions: NucleuxSuggestions(...)` |
| React Native | `SuggestedPrompt`; composer `suggestions={{ items, label, started }}` |

## Data

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | |
| `title` | A short action on something visible: "Find unresolved decisions". The accessible name |
| `prompt` | The fuller request placed in the field: "Find the unresolved decisions blocking the September release." |
| `description` | Optional, one line: what will happen. Shown in the list layout |

The set: `items` (at most four are shown), `label` (the set's accessible name, from its source: "Suggested for the September release"; not drawn), `started` (the conversation has begun), `after` (what the others do after a choice), `layout` (`chips` or `list`).

## Shared rules

`react-native/src/suggestedPrompts.ts` is the reference; `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/suggested-prompts.fixtures.json` (36 cases) and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

**How present the set is** (`suggestionsProminence(text, placed, started, after)`):

| Situation | Set |
|---|---|
| The conversation has started | **gone**, for good |
| Field empty (or only spaces) | **full** |
| The placed prompt, untouched | `stay` (default): **full**, the chosen one marked · `quiet`: **quiet**, the others as small plain chips under "Or start from" · `stepAside`: **hidden** |
| Anything the person wrote or edited | **hidden**: it steps aside so nothing can overwrite their words; clearing the field brings it back |

- **Never over someone's words** (`canPlaceSuggestion`): a pick lands only in an empty field or over the untouched placed prompt, which it replaces.
- **Marked** (`chosenSuggestion`): the suggestion whose prompt is in the field, untouched.
- **Shown** (`visibleSuggestions`): at most four; in quiet mode, not the one already in the field.
- **Announced** (polite): "“Find unresolved decisions” placed in the message field: Find the unresolved decisions blocking the September release. Edit it or send it."

## On choosing

1. The prompt replaces the field's text (only if `canPlace`), caret at the end.
2. Focus moves to the field.
3. The placement is announced.
4. Nothing is sent. From here it is ordinary composer text: edit, add context, change the model, voice, send.

## Look (Nucleux tokens)

- **Chips** (default): outlined, 32 visual, tap target 44pt (iOS) / 48dp (Android) as everywhere else, corner 8, 1pt `border`, title 14 medium `foreground`, optional 18 icon in `primary`. They wrap, 8 apart. The chosen one: `accent` fill and a `primary` outline, plus the selected state: a fill as well as a colour change (Nucleux has no secondary-container colour).
- **List**: rows at least 44pt / 48dp tall, title 14 medium, description 13 `mutedForeground`; chosen row `accent` fill.
- **Quiet**: "Or start from" in 12 `mutedForeground`, then the others as ghost chips (no outline).
- Under the composer, 8 below it, no wider than it.
- Appearing and stepping aside: immediate for now (see below).

## Accessibility

- The set is a group named by `label`, with no visible heading.
- Each suggestion is a button. Its name is the title; its hint is the description (if any) plus "Places the request in the message field, to edit before you send."
- The chosen one reports selected.
- When the set steps aside it leaves the accessibility tree and the focus order, not just the screen.

## Not in scope (later)

- Motion: the title flying into the field (the pattern's 420 ms hand-over) and the 300 ms collapse. Today the text is simply there and the set simply goes, which is also what reduced motion asks for.
- Compact cards and the sideways-scrolling row.
- Arrow keys between suggestions (Tab works).
- An optional "Started from a suggestion" line under the composer (off by default in the pattern).

components.specText:
# Autocomplete

The pattern library's **Autocomplete** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `autocomplete`; the engine `acComplete` / `acAttach` and demo provider in `material-sim.js`; CSS `.ac-ghost`, `.ac-menu`). It finishes the request someone is **already writing**: the likely rest of a familiar request after the caret, or a short menu after `/`, `@` or `#`. Accepting inserts ordinary, editable text. **Nothing is ever sent for them.**

A composer option, like suggestions: it attaches to the composer's field and adds nothing else.

| Platform | Names |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `.nucleuxAutocomplete(_ provider:)` on the composer |
| Compose | composer `autocomplete = NucleuxAutocompleteProvider(...)` |
| Flutter | composer `autocomplete: NucleuxAutocompleteProvider(...)` |
| React Native | composer `autocomplete={provider}` |

## Provider (from the host)

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `phrases` | Requests to complete, in the person's own phrasing |
| `minChars` | Characters typed before anything is offered. Default 8; the pattern's demo uses 10 |
| `triggers` | `/` commands, `@` mentions (people, files), `#` tools: each a list of items (`label`, optional `key` also matched, `description`, `insert`) |
| `enabled` | Turn a type off |

## Shared rules

`react-native/src/autocomplete.ts` is the reference (a port of the pattern's `acComplete`); `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/autocomplete.fixtures.json` (19 cases with the pattern's demo provider) and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

- **Inline:** only with the caret at the end, only after `minChars`, only a phrase that **continues the typed text exactly** (ignoring case; the typed text keeps its own case). The suggestion is the rest of the phrase.
- **It follows along** as the same words are typed, and **disappears the moment they diverge**.
- **Menus:** `/` only at the start of the request; `@` and `#` after a space or at the start (so `me@example` is not a mention). Items whose label or key starts with what follows the trigger, at most 6.
- **Accept** (`acceptCompletion`): inline appends the rest, caret at the end. A menu item replaces the trigger and query with `trigger + label` (or `insert`) and a space, keeping any text after the caret. Never sends.
- **One word** (`acceptCompletionWord`, ⌘/Ctrl + →): takes the next word.
- **Dismiss:** the phrase stays away (`keepDismissed`) while the typed text still leads into it; it's forgotten once they diverge.
- **Announced once** when a completion first appears (`sameCompletion` tells a followed-along one from a new one), never per keystroke:
  - "Suggestion: risks and group them by owner. Accept to use it."
  - "4 people and files. Choose one to insert."
  - "Accepted. Not sent — edit it or send it when you are ready." · "Inserted @Release plan. Not sent." · "Suggestion dismissed."

## On a phone (adapted from the pattern)

The pattern accepts with Tab and puts a "Tab" key at the end of the suggestion. A touch keyboard has no Tab, so:

| Pattern | Nucleux mobile |
|---|---|
| Rest of the request after the caret, lighter, outside the field's value | Same: drawn over the field in `mutedForeground`, hidden from screen readers |
| "Tab" key at its end; tap the suggestion to accept | An **Accept** chip in the composer's controls while there's a suggestion (44pt/48dp, spoken "Accept suggestion: …"). Its "Dismiss suggestion" is a screen-reader action |
| Tab / → / ⌘→ | Same, on hardware keyboards (SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter). Escape dismisses |
| `/` `@` `#` menu above the composer, focus stays in the field | Same: a list panel above the composer, not a modal; the field keeps focus. Heading Commands / Mention / Tools; rows at least 44pt / 48dp: `/summarize · Summarize a doc or thread`. Hardware: ↑ ↓ move, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes |
| Enter never accepts | Enter is still the composer's send key, except while a menu is open (it inserts) |

- **SwiftUI on iOS 17** can't read the caret, so completions are offered only for the end of the text (where typing happens).
- **React Native** has no hardware-key handling (see Open Input); touch only.

## Look

- Suggestion: the field's own font and size, `mutedForeground`; no fade (it is simply there, or gone).
- Accept chip: outlined, corner 8, "Accept" 13 medium with a check icon.
- Menu: the composer's panel style (background, 1pt border, corner 16), heading 11 uppercase `mutedForeground`, rows label 14 `foreground` + description 13 `mutedForeground`, the active row `accent`.

## Accessibility

- The suggestion is not in the field's value and not in the accessibility tree; it's announced in words instead.
- The Accept chip carries the suggestion in its label.
- Menu rows are buttons; the panel is named by its heading.

## Not in scope (later)

- The "menu" treatment for prompt completions (a single item in a menu instead of inline).
- Snoozing or a settings switch to turn suggestions off.

components.specText:
# Proactive Suggestions

The pattern library's **Proactive Suggestions** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `proactive`; the engine `proRender` / `proNotice` / `proResolve` / `proAct` and the release-readiness scenario in `material-sim.js`; CSS `.md-pro`). The agent **noticed something** during the work and offers **one** next step, with the reason. It is a recommendation, never an action taken.

| Platform | Names |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxProactiveController` (`@Observable`), `NucleuxProactiveSuggestion`, `NucleuxProactiveReview` |
| Compose | `NucleuxProactiveController`, `rememberNucleuxProactiveController`, `NucleuxProactiveSuggestion`, `NucleuxProactiveReview` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxProactiveController` (`ChangeNotifier`), `NucleuxProactiveSuggestion`, `NucleuxProactiveReview` |
| React Native | `useProactiveSuggestion`, `ProactiveSuggestion`, `ProactiveReview` |

## What the host supplies

| | Notes |
|---|---|
| `agent` | "Aria" |
| `reason` | The evidence, specifically: counts, names, dates. "QA is signed off, but two high-priority blockers still have no owner." |
| `action` | A recommendation, never past tense: "Assign owners before the release?" |
| `primary` | Opens the review. Default "Review" |
| `snoozeLabel` | With one, the card offers a snooze: "Remind me tomorrow" |
| `dismissible` | Default true |
| `resolved` | Said when the reason goes away. Default "Resolved — nothing to do." |
| **Observations** | `notice(evidence, now)` whenever what it watches changes: a key for the facts ("ONB-112,EXP-210"), or none when the reason is gone |
| **Review** | The host's own workflow (the proposal, changeable) inside `ProactiveReview`, with one confirming action. On confirm: `confirmed("2 owners assigned")` |

## The state machine

`react-native/src/proactive.ts` is the reference (a port of the pattern's engine); `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/proactive.fixtures.json` (12 event sequences, every step's state, view and announcement) and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

| Phase | Shown | Announced (politely) |
|---|---|---|
| dormant | nothing | |
| suggested | the card: "Suggested by Aria", reason, action · **Review** · *Remind me tomorrow* · *Dismiss* | "Suggestion from Aria: {reason} {action} Nothing has changed." |
| preparing | the card with "Preparing a review — nothing has changed yet." | |
| review | the card, and the host's review below it | "Review opened. Nothing changes until you confirm." |
| dismissed | status line "Dismissed. Aria won’t suggest this again unless something changes." · Undo | the same |
| snoozed | status line "Snoozed until tomorrow, 9:00." · Undo | the same |
| resolved | the card says the `resolved` line, then goes (2.4 s) | "The suggestion no longer applies." |
| after confirming | status line "2 owners assigned — you confirmed Aria’s proposal." (· Undo if the host can) | the same |

Rules:

- **Raised only on evidence.** It never appears on a timer.
- **Dismiss is remembered for that evidence.** The same facts never bring it back, a day later included; only new facts do.
- **Snooze** hides it until a time and brings it back only if it's still true.
- **It withdraws when the reason goes away,** saying so. A snoozed or dismissed one whose reason has gone is quietly forgotten, and Undo can't revive it.
- **Nothing changes until the person confirms** in the review. Cancel goes back to the suggestion.

The dismiss wording is generic ("unless something changes"); the pattern's demo says "for these issues".

## Look

- Card, placed by the host next to what it's about (inline), or at the bottom of the surface (floating). Never a dialog; it doesn't take focus.
- `tonal` (default): `accent` fill. `outlined`: 1pt `border`. Corner 16, padding 14 (compact 10).
- Provenance: the generated mark (Lucide `badge-info`, 16, `mutedForeground`) and "Suggested by Aria", 12 `mutedForeground`. While it applies, the turning working mark beside the status line.
- Reason 13 `mutedForeground`; action 15 semibold `foreground`.
- Actions: the primary as a small primary Button; snooze and dismiss as small ghost Buttons.
- Preparing: the working mark (`loader-circle`) and the line. Resolved: `circle-check` and the line.
- Review: an outlined card under the suggestion: title 15 semibold, "Proposed by Aria. Nothing changes until you confirm." with the generated mark, the host's content, then the confirming Button and Cancel.
- No rise or fade yet (see below).

## Accessibility

- The card is a region named "Suggestion from Aria"; the review is a region named by its title.
- Nothing steals focus when it appears; every change is announced politely.
- Every action is a real button with a 44pt / 48dp target; Undo sits in the status line right after.

## Not in scope (later)

- The 400 ms rise and the 2 s fade; "at the next pause" timing (the host decides when to call `notice`).
- Per-kind settings (turning a kind of suggestion off).

review cancelled goes back to the suggestion

dismissed, then new evidence raises it again

the reason goes away: resolved, then gone

components.specText:
# Disclosure and Caveat

Two Trust & Disclosure patterns from the pattern library (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `disclosure` with examples `list-item-chip`, `basic-dialog`, `field-banner`, `banner`; `caveat` with `below-input`, `output-footer`, `on-action`, `specific`; simulators in `material-sim.js`). Both are words that **travel with generated content**. **Caveat is rebuilt (22 Oct) from the library's 16 Oct revision: see `specs/caveat.md`.** The Caveat section below is the old standing line, kept as history; the library now forbids it.

The wording lives in `react-native/src/trust.ts`; `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/trust.fixtures.json` and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## Disclosure

Revised 22 Oct from the library's 16 Oct revision (backlog item 6). **Makes it clear where AI is involved, at the point it matters, with three meanings kept apart**, each with its own mark, words and place:

| Meaning | What the kit shows | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **AI action** (a control that will run AI on something) | The action's mark and verb ("Rewrite"), and **once it applies to something, one line before it runs**: "**Rewrite with AI.** Aria rewrites the Highlights paragraph. You review the result before it replaces your text." (`AiActionNote`) | Beside the control |
| **AI working** | The working mark, the doing words and **Stop** (`AiWorkingStatus`, `specs/ai-marks.md`) | On the content being worked on |
| **AI-generated content** | **"Generated with AI"** attached to the content it describes, opening in place to: **What Aria did**, **What it used**, **Not checked**, and **Your original** ("Kept. Undo brings it back.", with Show original) or, in someone else's view, **Kept by** ("Jordan, 10:42"). Undo for the person who asked (`GeneratedLabel`, `GeneratedResult`, `GeneratedValue`) | On the content, for as long as it is on the page, for the colleague who opens it later too |

Rules:

- **Only what AI touched is labelled.** An agent's turn says who it is, **"AI agent"** (`AgentTag`, the identity chip's words), not "generated": the label goes on content AI wrote or changed. Two paragraphs by people carry nothing.
- **The host words the details**, specifically: what the agent did (and did not add), what it used (with counts), what nobody checked (with where a figure came from). The kit never says **"verified"** (nor "fact-checked", "accurate"); a fixture test fails if any wording does.
- **Same words and marks everywhere**, never colour or an icon alone; the generated mark comes from the AI marks table.

| Component | Use | Look |
|---|---|---|
| `DisclosureChip` | "Generated with AI" as a plain label (no details) | `accent` fill, radius 6, the generated mark 14 in `primary`, 12 medium `foreground`, 22 tall. Not a button |
| `GeneratedLabel` | The label that opens to the details (`agent`, `noun`, `details`, `onUndo`) | Outlined chip with a chevron, a 44 / 48 target; details in a 1 `border` box, radius 12, padding 12: label 12 semibold `mutedForeground`, value 13 |
| `AgentTag` | "AI agent" on agent turns and identity rows | `muted` fill, 12 medium `mutedForeground`, no mark |
| `AgentMessage` / `PersonMessage` | Avatar, name, the tag (agents only), time, then the text | Agent avatar a **rounded square**, a person's a **circle** |
| `GeneratedValue` | A value the agent drafted inside a human surface; the label sits inside the field, opening to `details` when given | Field: label 12 muted, value 15, 1 `border`, radius 12; foot: the label, then the host's actions |
| `AiActionNote` | The one-line explanation of an action once it applies to something | The action mark 14 in `brand`, 13 with the title semibold |
| `DisclosureBanner`, `DisclosureIntro` | Unchanged: a standing notice in a workspace, and the first-run introduction | |

Spoken: an agent header reads "Aria, AI agent, 10:24" (the separators matter); a person's "Dana Khoury, 9:41"; a generated value "Reply to Dana, generated with AI by Aria" before its text; the label "Generated with AI", collapsed or expanded; the details region "About this paragraph", each row "Not checked: …".

Ours, not the library's: "AI agent" on turns (the library's identity label, used where the old chip was), the spoken forms, and Undo beside the label rather than in a separate bar.

**Before 22 Oct** every agent turn carried "AI generated" and a drafted value said "Drafted by Aria"; the library now labels only AI-touched content, with "Generated with AI".

## Caveat (until 22 Oct; removed)

The kit had a standing "Aria can make mistakes. Check anything important before you use it." under the composer, a boxed "Generated summary — verify before sharing." under output, and "Output may be inaccurate — check it before you send." as the hint on a generate action. The library's 16 Oct revision forbids generic warnings ("teaches people to ignore it, and says nothing about the answer in front of them"), so all three are gone, and the disclosure intro no longer says answers "can be wrong". A specific limitation of one result is a Caveat attached to it: `specs/caveat.md`.

## Not in scope (later)

- The chip opening into a panel (the pattern's motion note).
- The chip settling in with its content (motion).

components.specSummary:
The pattern library's **Caveat** pattern as revised on 16 Oct 2026 (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `caveat`; the Fieldnotes simulator in `material-sim.js`). It replaces the standing "can make mistakes" line the kit had before (`specs/disclosure-and-caveat.md`, now history).

A caveat **says what is incomplete, uncertain or out of date about this result**, attached to it, with why that matters and a next step. It appears only when there is a real limitation, and leaves when the reason is gone. # Caveat

The pattern library's **Caveat** pattern as revised on 16 Oct 2026 (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `caveat`; the Fieldnotes simulator in `material-sim.js`). It replaces the standing "can make mistakes" line the kit had before (`specs/disclosure-and-caveat.md`, now history).

A caveat **says what is incomplete, uncertain or out of date about this result**, attached to it, with why that matters and a next step. It appears only when there is a real limitation, and leaves when the reason is gone. A generic "AI can make mistakes" on every answer teaches people to skip it and says nothing about the answer in front of them, so the kit no longer has one: no composer caveat, no "verify before sharing", no caveat on a generate button.

Kinds of limitation it names (the host words them, with the specifics: the count, the source, the date):

- incomplete context: "2 of 8 interviews could not be opened, so this summary reflects 6."
- uncertainty: a finding rests on two interviews
- stale information: a source last updated three months ago
- an omission: private channels are not included
- a capability limit: drafted, but it can't be sent until email is connected

The rules and words live in `react-native/src/caveatRules.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/caveat.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## What the host supplies

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | The gap, specifically | "2 of 8 interviews could not be opened, so this summary reflects 6." |
| `why` | Why it matters for this result | "Themes raised only in those two calls are missing, not just under-counted." |
| `short` | The gap in a few words, for the announcement | "2 of 8 interviews could not be opened." |
| `noun` | What the result is | "summary" |
| `sources` (optional) | Behind Review sources: each source, read or not and why | "Hana Kim · Oct 3", "Not opened — the file was moved" |
| `recover` (optional) | The step that removes the reason: its label, what is said while it runs, and what is said when it worked | "Reconnect", "Reconnecting to Research › October…", "Both interviews are available again." |

The host runs the recovery and the update (the kit asks with `request: 'recover'` / `'update'`) and answers `recovered`, `recoverFailed` or `updated` with what changed.

## Limitation → explanation → recovery → resolution

| State | Shown | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Gap | The result as it is (never withheld), with the note attached: info mark, `message`, `why`; **Review sources** (opens the source list; then **Hide sources**) and the recovery (**Reconnect**) | "Summary ready, with a caveat: 2 of 8 interviews could not be opened." (the host says it with the result) |
| Recovering | A progress line with `recover.busy`; Reconnect is unavailable | "Reconnecting to Research › October…" |
| Recovery failed | The gap again, with "Couldn’t reconnect. Nothing changed; try again, or review the sources." | the same |
| Ready | "Both interviews are available again." and **Update the summary**. **Nothing reruns on its own**: the person chooses | "Both interviews are available again. Update the summary when you are ready." |
| Updating | "Updating the summary…" | the same |
| Resolved | The note turns into what changed: a check, "All 8 interviews read — summary updated", "One theme was added from the two calls that were missing.", **Dismiss**. The host marks the changed line **Updated**, once | "All 8 interviews read. Summary updated: one theme added." |
| Gone | Nothing: no standing warning stays behind | "Caveat dismissed." |

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Gap note | `muted` fill, radius 12, padding 12; `info` 16 in `foreground`; message 14 medium `foreground`, why 13 `mutedForeground`; actions as ghost small buttons (44 / 48 targets) |
| Sources | Rows inside the note: `circle-check` or `triangle-alert` 14 in `mutedForeground`, the name 13 medium, the note 12 `mutedForeground` |
| Progress | The kit's working mark and the line, 13 `mutedForeground` |
| Resolved note | `background` with a 1 `border` outline, `circle-check` 16 |
| Updated mark | `rotate-cw` 12 and "Updated", 11 semibold `mutedForeground` |

Caution, not alarm: never the error colour, no motion beyond the note appearing with the result, never behind a hover (phones have none).

## Accessibility

- The note is a group named "Caveat about this summary", read after the result; each source row is read as one line ("Hana Kim · Oct 3, Not opened — the file was moved").
- Review sources says whether it is open. Every change is announced politely; focus stays where it is.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- The failure of the recovery and its wording (the simulator only draws success).
- The progress line while updating (the simulator shows the agent's working turn, which is the host's).
- `short` and `noun` as separate host words, so the kit can build the announcements and labels.

## Not in scope (later)

- More than one caveat on a result (the host shows the most important).
- Caveats on a field or a draft inside an editor (the pattern's examples are all results in a conversation).

components.specText:
# Consent

The pattern library's **Consent** pattern as revised on 16 Oct 2026 (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `consent`; the Cadence simulator in `material-sim.js`). **Asks before the agent accesses something sensitive or takes an important action**: what, why this task needs it, the scope, and two real choices. Nothing happens before the answer, and no answer costs the person their work.

It is raised by the work itself, at the step that needs it: data access (read Google Drive for this request), a consequential action (create three GitHub issues), or an ongoing permission (use project files in future conversations). Ask again only when something changed (it expired, or what is being approved is different) and say why.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/consent.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/consent.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

**Replaced (22 Oct):** the multi-switch request that pre-switched the needed sources on ("Allow selected"), the gap note, and the inline "Allow once · Always allow · Decline" ask. The library now asks for nothing preselected and two equal answers. `GrantedList`, the standing view of what the agent can see, stays.

## What the host supplies

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| `agent`, `resource` | Who asks, for what | "Aria", "Google Drive" |
| `why` | Why this task needs it | "The product brief is in Google Drive. Aria needs to read it to compare it with this meeting." |
| `scope` | Plain lines: `can`, `cannot`, `duration` | "Read files and folders your account can open", "Can’t edit, share or delete anything", "For this conversation only" |
| `then` | What happens if they continue | "Google Drive asks you to confirm your account, then Aria reads only the brief and finishes the comparison." |
| `details` (optional) | Behind Review details | Account, Activity ("Every file Aria opens is listed in this conversation."), Turn it off ("From this conversation, or Settings › Connected apps.") |
| `alternatives` (optional) | Other ways to finish after Not now | "Continue without Drive", "Add the brief as a file" |
| `granted` | The line once allowed | "Google Drive connected for this conversation. Aria can read files your account can open." |
| `expiresAfterDays`, `alreadyRead` (optional) | For the expired request and the revoked note | 30; "The brief I already read is quoted above and stays in this conversation." |

The host connects (the kit asks with `request: 'connect'` and gets `connected` or `connectFailed`), resumes the original task (`request: 'resume'`), revokes (`request: 'revoke'`), and runs an alternative when it is chosen. The agent's own sentence before the card ("I’ve read the meeting. The product brief is in Google Drive, which I can’t open yet.") is the host's.

## States

| State | Shown | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Asking | A card: **Access request**, the resource's mark, "Allow Aria to use Google Drive?", `why`; "What Aria will be able to do" and the scope lines; "**If you continue:** …"; **Review details** (opens the details; then **Hide details**); **Not now** and **Continue**, the same size and weight, nothing preselected | "Aria needs your permission to use Google Drive." |
| Connecting | "Connecting to Google Drive…" with the working mark; the answers go | "Connecting to Google Drive." |
| Connect failed | The request again, with "Couldn’t connect to Google Drive. Nothing was opened." | the same |
| Approved | `granted`, with **Turn off**. The original task resumes on its own: the person asked once | "Google Drive connected." |
| Denied | "Okay — I won’t use Google Drive, and nothing was opened. Your request is kept. Here are two other ways to finish it." then the alternatives and **Allow Google Drive** | "Google Drive not allowed. Your request is kept." |
| Expired | The request with **Needs approval again**, "Google Drive access has expired", "You allowed Google Drive 30 days ago. Access ends after 30 days so it doesn’t stay on indefinitely.", and **Allow again** | "Google Drive access has expired. Aria needs your permission again." |
| Revoked | "Google Drive turned off. I can’t open anything new from it." and `alreadyRead`; **Allow Google Drive** | "Google Drive turned off." |

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Request card | `background`, 1 `border`, radius 16, padding 16; the badge 11 semibold `mutedForeground`; title 17 semibold; why 14 `mutedForeground`; "What Aria will be able to do" 12 semibold; each scope line an `eye` / `ban` / `clock` 16 in `mutedForeground` and 14 `foreground`; "If you continue:" 13 with the label semibold |
| Answers | Two buttons of the same size (`sm`, secondary): neither colour makes one answer look safer than the other |
| Details | Rows: label 12 semibold `mutedForeground`, value 13 `foreground` |
| Approved | `muted` row, radius 12: the resource's line 13 and a ghost **Turn off** |
| Denied / revoked | The agent's text 14, then the alternatives as secondary buttons, and Allow as ghost |

Stable and quiet: the card appears once and holds still; the outcome replaces it without moving the conversation.

## Accessibility

- The request is a group named by its title; Review details says whether it is open.
- Continue and Not now are real buttons with full targets, side by side; neither is focused for the person.
- Every outcome is announced politely; focus stays where it is.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- The connection failure and its wording.
- "I can’t open anything new from it." for the revoked note (the simulator says "new files from Drive"; the kit doesn't know what the resource holds).
- One connecting line (the simulator also shows "Google Drive is confirming your account…" first; that step is the resource's own sign-in).
- Answers as two secondary buttons (the pattern's action confirmation colours Continue; equal weight is its rule).

## GrantedList (unchanged)

- Several resources in one request (ask for each when its step is reached).
- The resource's own sign-in screen (the host's).
