components.specText:
# Connect Data Source

The pattern library's **Connect Data Source** pattern (branch-2: `material-patterns.js` → `connectors`; `material-connect.js` for the states, the card, the list, Manage and disconnect; the simulator in `material-sim.js`). **Grant the agent standing access to a service it needs.** An account, not a file: the access outlives the conversation and can be withdrawn.

It is not an MCP server. A data source is one named account with a bounded scope list the **product** writes, in plain verbs, and shows **before** the handoff; never a discovered tool list. Read and search by default; write, if a product ever wants it, is a second and separate question.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/connectSource.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/connect-source.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

| Platform | Names |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `NucleuxConnectCard`, `NucleuxConnectSources`, `NucleuxConnectManage`, `NucleuxConnectChip`; `NucleuxConnect` |
| Compose | `NucleuxConnectCard`, `NucleuxConnectSources`, `NucleuxConnectManage`, `NucleuxConnectChip`; `NucleuxConnect` |
| Flutter | `NucleuxConnectCard`, `NucleuxConnectSources`, `NucleuxConnectManage`, `NucleuxConnectChip`; `NucleuxConnect` |
| React Native | `ConnectCard`, `ConnectSources`, `ConnectManage`, `ConnectChip`; `cardActions`, `connectRowLine`… |

## What the host supplies

- **Each service**, all of it written by the product: `{ id, name, mark, purpose, blurb, account, readOnly, benefits[], canSee[], useLine }`. `benefits` is the scope list before the handoff (`{ icon: search | doc | code | chat | shield, title, what }`); `canSee` is Manage's list.
- **The service's own logo**, optionally (a view the host draws unaltered). Without one, a two-letter tile in Nucleux's own type.
- **The state** of each connection, which the host drives: `available`, `authorise`, `connecting`, `connected`, `active`, `limited`, `stale`, `error`, `blocked`.
- **The handoff itself.** The kit never draws a sign-in or a password field: a connector that imitates the provider's sign-in teaches people the shape every credential-phishing page uses. **Continue to Google Drive** is the host's cue to open the provider (a web authentication session), and the card waits.
- Callbacks for each action, the switch, Manage's Disconnect (after the kit has asked), and the chip.

## States

| State | Says | Live | Card actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `available` | Not connected | | **Connect**, then the handoff sentence |
| `authorise` | Needs your approval | | The setup surface: **Continue to {name}**, Not now |
| `connecting` | Waiting for the service… | | The same surface, mid-transition: Cancel |
| `connected` | Connected | yes | Manage |
| `active` | Using now | yes | Manage; the line becomes the activity |
| `limited` | Connected, read only | yes | Manage |
| `stale` | Reconnect required | | **Reconnect**, Manage |
| `error` | Couldn't reach it | | **Try again**, Cancel |
| `blocked` | Turned off by your organization | | Ask an admin. **No Connect**: pressing it could never work |

The word comes first after the name, then the account ("Connected · j.rivera@northwind.example"): "connected as whom" is the question people actually have. Live states get a dot **beside** the word, never instead of it.

## The card

- **Inline** (in a conversation), it opens with the reason: what the agent can't reach and why it stopped. The host writes the wall ("The research you're asking about is in files I've never been given. Connecting Google Drive lets me read the ones you can already open."); for an expired sign-in or an unreachable service the kit has the sentence ("The sign-in to Google Drive has expired, so I stopped rather than answering from memory." / "Google Drive didn't answer. Nothing was granted, and nothing was sent.").
- **Setup** (authorise, connecting): one quiet surface for deciding and for watching the handoff. "Connect Google Drive", the blurb, then the scope list as rows (an icon, the verb in semibold, what it covers): Search your files, Read file contents, **You stay in control**. **Continue to Google Drive** (with the external-link icon), **Not now**, and "You sign in with Google Drive. Access can be withdrawn at any time." Connecting is the same surface: "Connecting Google Drive…", "Signing in and checking access.", the working mark round the tile, and only Cancel; it is announced, because it resolves while the person is in the provider's window.
- **Status** (everything else): the head, one sentence (the use line, "Reconnect to carry on using Google Drive in this conversation.", "This happens. Trying again usually works.", the blocked line, or the read-only line), and the actions. While **active**, the sentence is the activity: "Searching Google Drive…", "Reading 5 relevant files…", then "Reviewed 5 relevant files in Google Drive". No percentage.

## The list

Connected first, then available; derived from each item, so no row can be in both, and an empty group isn't drawn. Each group is labelled ("Connected sources", "Available sources") for assistive technology; the headings are drawn on request.

- A **connected** row has a switch, "Google Drive available to the agent". Off keeps the grant, the account and the configuration; ending a connection is Manage's job. The line is the account, or "Not available to the agent" when off, or "Reconnect required · account" with a **Reconnect** button.
- An **available** row has a quiet **Connect** (spoken "Connect Slack"); a failed one **Try again**; a blocked one **Ask an admin**; a connecting one "Waiting for Slack…" and no button.
- Tapping a connected row opens Manage.

## Manage and disconnect

Manage (in a sheet the host presents) is one glance: the head, "The agent can use:" and the `canSee` list, "Read only — nothing here can be changed by the agent." when it is, then Reconnect (if stale), **Disconnect** and **Done**. Disconnect asks first, inside the sheet: "Disconnect Google Drive?" / "The agent will no longer be able to use Google Drive information in new requests. Nothing already said in this conversation is removed." **Cancel** first, then **Disconnect** (destructive).

## The chip

Above the composer, one per **usable** source (granted, switched on, not expired): the tile, the name and "search · read" (or "read only"). A source switched off or expired leaves the composer: a chip that outlives its grant lies. Tapping opens Manage. Spoken: "Data source: Google Drive, search and read. Opens Manage."

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Card | `background`, 1pt `border`, corner 16, padding 16, gap 12. Inline: `muted` fill, no border, because it belongs to the agent's turn |
| Reason | 14 `foreground` |
| Tile | 40 × 40, corner 10, `background` with 1pt `border` (a logo keeps its own colours on it); monogram 13 bold `foreground` |
| Name, meta | 15 semibold; 12 `mutedForeground`; dot 8 `success` |
| Setup | Centred tile 56 (the working mark rings it while connecting), title 20 semibold, lede 14 `mutedForeground`; scope rows with an 18 icon in `primary`, title 14 semibold, what 13 `mutedForeground`; the two buttons full width (md), the handoff line 12 `mutedForeground` centred |
| Activity | 13, a pulsing 8 `brand` dot; done: `check` in `success` |
| List | 1pt `border`, corner 16; rows at least 56 with dividers; tile 32; name 15 medium, line 13 `mutedForeground`; the Nucleux switch; a 1pt divider between groups |
| Manage | Head, then 14 body; bullets 6 `mutedForeground`; read-only line 13 with `lock` |
| Chip | Height 32, fully rounded, `accent` fill, tile 20, name 13 semibold, detail 12 `mutedForeground`, `chevron-down` |

## Accessibility

- The status is a word before it is a dot; the head reads "Google Drive, Connected, j.rivera@northwind.example".
- Every action names its outcome and the service: "Connect Google Drive", "Sign in to Google Drive again", "Try connecting Google Drive again", "Manage Google Drive".
- The scope list is a list; each row reads "Search your files: files and folders you can already open."
- Changes are announced politely: connecting, connected, not connected (cancel), failed, sign-in expired, switched off and on, disconnected, still connected.
- The disconnect question is announced and Cancel comes first.
- Under Reduce Motion the card arrives at once and nothing pulses.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **No logos ship with the kit.** The pattern draws each service's own mark; a native kit can't bundle other companies' logos, so the host passes one in, and without it a monogram tile stands in.
- **The handoff is the host's.** Continue opens nothing by itself; the host opens the provider and drives the state.
- **The spoken labels** for actions ("Sign in to Google Drive again"), rows, benefits and the chip, and every announcement.
- **Blocked has a sentence** ("Your organization has turned Google Drive off for everyone. An admin can turn it back on."), and **limited** adds "It can't change anything." to the use line.
- **The failed row's line**, "Couldn't reach it. Nothing was granted."
- **Manage's confirm sits inside the sheet** rather than over it, as Knowledge Base's remove does.
- **Spelling:** "organization".

## Not in scope (later)

- The **Access changed** state (a grant that narrowed), and the **Suggested** and **Administered** variants: the host's, from the same words.
- A write-access ladder (Always ask / Allow read / Allow all): the pattern asks for read only.

components.specText:
# Modes

The pattern library's **Modes** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `modes`; the preview and states in `material-preview.js`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). **Choose how the agent approaches the task**: Brainstorm, Draft, Review, Plan. It is shown in the composer and kept separate from the model.

A mode changes how the agent works (different steps, tools or output). It is not a label over the same behaviour, and it doesn't stand in for the model or reasoning effort: the model chip beside it is a different choice. **Changing mode never touches the prompt text, the model or the context.**

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/modes.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/modes.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## Request settings: the tune control

Modes introduces the composer's **settings** option. Since the library's update of 21 Oct 2026, settings are reached through **one tune control** (`sliders-horizontal`, an icon button right after +), not chips in the composer. Voice & Tone, Preset Styles and Prompt Enhancer use the same control.

- **Its menu** (in the menu surface): a row per setting with its icon, its name and its value on the right, or the empty word while nothing is chosen ("Mode · None", "Tone · Default", "Style · Normal"); a set value is `primary` and semibold. When the composer has Prompt Enhancer, a last row **Improve prompt** (the AI action mark), which reads "Improving…" and stops it while it works. Rows are 48 tall, read "Mode: Plan".
- **Choosing a row** closes the menu and opens that setting's picker from the same control. Every picker has a close × in its head (no chip beside it to close it with).
- **Nothing sits in the composer up front.** A dot on the control (`primary`, ringed in `background`) shows that something is on, and its name says what: "Request settings", or "Request settings: Mode Plan, Tone Professional". It is unavailable while the agent works.
- **Clearing** is in each picker: No mode, Default voice, or the Normal style.

A setting is `{ id, label, icon, value?, valueIcon?, empty, hint, picker(close), pickerLabel, onOpenChange?, note?, noteAction? }`. Focus goes back to the field when a picker closes.

## The picker

- **Title** "Mode", and "How Aria approaches this request. Model and effort stay as they are."
- One row per mode, a radio group: the icon, the name, what changes, and a check on the chosen one. Read aloud: "Plan. Break the work into steps with owners and dates."
- **An unavailable mode** is listed with its reason, at reduced emphasis and marked disabled: "Research. Gather and compare information from the web, with sources. Unavailable: Not available in this workspace — web access is turned off." Choosing it doesn't apply it. The picker stays open and says "Research isn’t available here. Choose another mode." A host can leave unavailable modes out instead.
- **No mode**, a text button at the foot, when a mode is chosen and clearing is allowed.
- A close × in the head.

## What happens

| Event | Result | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Choose | Picker closes; the menu row and the control's name carry the mode | "Mode: Plan. Break the work into steps with owners and dates. Your text is unchanged." |
| Switch to another | The same, plus a line under the composer: "Mode changed to Review. Your text is unchanged." | as above |
| Choose an unavailable one | Not applied; picker stays open with the reason | "Research isn’t available here. Choose another mode." |
| No mode | The menu row reads "Mode · None" | "No mode. Your text is unchanged." |
| Send | The mode stays until changed | "Sent in Plan mode. It stays until you change it." |

After sending, the request carries a small tag with the mode, and the agent's header reads "Aria · Plan mode".

## What the host supplies

The modes it genuinely supports (`{ id, name, description, icon?, unavailable? }`; `DEFAULT_MODES` is the pattern's five), the current mode (controlled), and whether it can be cleared. The host sends the mode with the request as a setting; the kit never edits the text.

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Tune control | An icon button after +; the dot 8 across at its top right |
| Menu rows | 48 tall: 18 icon, 15 label, the value 13 on the right (`mutedForeground`, or `primary` semibold when set) |
| Picker | The menu surface; title 15 semibold, subtitle 13 `mutedForeground`; rows at least 56 with a 20 icon, name 14 medium, description 13 `mutedForeground`, the reason 12 `mutedForeground` italic; chosen row `accent` with `check`; unavailable at 55% |
| Refusal | `info` icon, 13 `foreground`, on `muted` |
| Changed note | Under the composer, 12 `mutedForeground` with `rotate-cw` |
| Tag on a sent request | `muted` chip, 11 semibold |

## Accessibility

- The picker is a radio group; each option says what it changes, and an unavailable one says why and is marked disabled.
- Every change is announced politely and says the text is unchanged; nothing takes focus away from the person.
- The tune control's name says what is on; each menu row says its value.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **The tune control** follows the library's 21 Oct update; the earlier chip row is gone.
- **The spoken labels** "Request settings: Mode Plan" and "Mode: Plan".
- **Icons:** `sliders-horizontal` for Mode, `file-text` for Draft, `eye` for Review (Lucide's nearest to the pattern's Material symbols).

## Not in scope (later)

- A default mode per workspace (the host passes it as the starting value).
- The compact picker density.

components.specText:
# Voice & Tone

The pattern library's **Voice & Tone** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `voice-tone`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). **Say how the reply should sound**: Professional, Friendly, Conversational, Formal, or your own words. It shows in the composer and is sent with the request as a setting.

Tone changes wording, never facts. The same update reads differently to leadership and to customers, and keeping tone apart from content means changing it can't quietly change what is said. **Choosing a tone never edits the prompt.** It is for writing tasks where the audience changes the voice: updates, replies, announcements. It isn't for analysis or lookups, and it isn't the agent's standing personality (that is Personality).

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/tone.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/voice-tone.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## In the tune control

Tone is a row of the composer's tune control (`specs/modes.md`, Request settings): "Tone · Default" until chosen, then "Tone · Professional"; the picker has a close × and, once a tone is chosen, **Default voice**, which removes it (with Undo). The chip table below is kept for the wording the setting still uses.

### The chip (before 21 Oct)

Tone uses the composer's setting chip from Modes (`specs/modes.md`), with the `message-square` icon.

| | Text | Read aloud |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing chosen | "Tone" | "Tone", hint "Choose how the reply should sound" |
| Chosen | "Tone · Professional" and × | "Tone: Professional. Change", and × "Remove tone Professional" |
| Described | "Tone · Custom" and × | "Tone: Custom. Change" |

## The picker

- **Title** "Tone", and "How the reply should sound. What it says stays the same."
- One row per tone, a radio group: the name, how it sounds, and a check on the chosen one. Read aloud with its sample: "Professional. Clear and measured. Sample: “Onboarding now takes one step instead of three.”"
- **A recommended tone** (the host's, optional) carries a quiet tag with its reason, "Recommended for stakeholders", and the reason is read with it. It is **never chosen for them**.
- **The sample** under the list: "Sample · Professional" and the quoted sentence. It shows the chosen tone's sample, else the recommended one's, else the first. The pattern previews the tone in focus; a phone has no pointer, so each option says its sample aloud and the visible sample follows the choice. A described tone has no sample.
- **Or describe a tone**: a field (placeholder "For example: warm but brief") with **Use this tone**, and "Best effort: the wording follows your description as closely as it can." An empty description does nothing.

## What happens

| Event | Result | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Choose | Picker closes, chip names the tone | "Tone: Professional. Clear and measured. What the reply says stays the same." |
| Switch to another | The same, plus a line under the composer with **Undo**: "Tone changed to Conversational. What the reply says stays the same." | as above |
| Describe | Chip reads "Tone · Custom" | "Tone: your own, “warm but brief”. Best effort. What the reply says stays the same." |
| Remove (×) | Chip goes back to "Tone"; a line with **Undo**: "Tone removed. Replies use the default voice." | "Tone removed. Replies use the default voice." |
| Undo | The previous tone (or the default voice) comes back; the line goes | "Tone back to Professional." / "Back to the default voice." |
| Send | The tone stays until changed; the line and Undo go | "Sent with Professional tone. It stays until you change it." |

After sending, the request carries a small tag with the tone ("Professional", or "Custom"), and the agent's header reads "Aria · Professional", or "Aria · Default voice" with none.

## What the host supplies

The tones it supports (`{ id, name, description, sample }`; `DEFAULT_TONES` is the pattern's four), an optional recommendation `{ id, reason }`, and the current choice (controlled: `{ tone, custom }`). The host sends the tone, and a described tone's words, with the request as a setting; the kit never edits the text.

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | At least 56, name 14 medium, description 13 `mutedForeground`, the recommendation tag 11 semibold on `muted`, led by the generated mark 11; chosen row `accent` with `check`. No colour per tone, no icons per tone |
| Sample | 11 semibold `mutedForeground` head, then the quoted sentence 14 `foreground`, on `muted`, radius 10 |
| Describe | The kit's text field, the help line 12 `mutedForeground`, **Use this tone** a secondary small button |
| Note with Undo | Under the composer, 12 `mutedForeground`; Undo a text button with a 44 / 48 target |

## Accessibility

- The picker is a radio group; each option says how it sounds and its sample, and the recommendation is read as part of the option, never as a selection.
- Every change is announced politely and says the content stays the same; nothing takes focus away from the person.
- Undo is a real button with its own name, beside the line it undoes.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **The sample follows the choice**, not the focus (no pointer on a phone); every option reads its sample aloud.
- **The recommendation tag carries the generated mark** (`badge-info` 11, since 22 Oct when generated content got its own glyph), with its words.
- **Undo on a note under the composer**, for switches and removal (the pattern asks for Undo without drawing it). The note's Undo is available to every composer setting.
- **"Custom"** as the chip's value for a described tone, and the spoken labels.
- **Icon:** `message-square` (Lucide's nearest to the pattern's Material `forum`).

## Not in scope (later)

- Asking for "another version" in a new tone (the host's request; the simulator's button is a prompt the host writes).
- Saving a described tone for next time (that is Preset Styles).

components.specSummary:
The pattern library's **Preset Styles** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `preset-styles`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). Modelled on Claude's styles: **named styles for how replies are written** (Normal, Concise, Formal, Explanatory, or one made from the person's own writing), previewed, and switchable mid-conversation.

A style is about how the agent writes, not what it knows or which model answers. It applies to new messages, edits and retries; **earlier replies keep the style they were written in**, and **the request text is never edited**. It is for people who return to the same kind of reply (summaries, customer emails, explanations for newcomers), not for one-off instructions.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/presetStyles.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/preset-styles.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.
components.specText:
# Preset Styles

The pattern library's **Preset Styles** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `preset-styles`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). Modelled on Claude's styles: **named styles for how replies are written** (Normal, Concise, Formal, Explanatory, or one made from the person's own writing), previewed, and switchable mid-conversation.

A style is about how the agent writes, not what it knows or which model answers. It applies to new messages, edits and retries; **earlier replies keep the style they were written in**, and **the request text is never edited**. It is for people who return to the same kind of reply (summaries, customer emails, explanations for newcomers), not for one-off instructions.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/presetStyles.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/preset-styles.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## In the tune control

Style is a row of the composer's tune control (`specs/modes.md`, Request settings): "Style · Normal" until another is chosen; choosing Normal in the picker goes back, with Undo. The picker has a close ×.

### The chip (before 21 Oct)

Style uses the composer's setting chip from Modes (`specs/modes.md`), with the `pen-line` icon. **Normal is always there and one tap away**: with Normal the chip reads "Style" with no ×.

| | Text | Read aloud |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | "Style" | "Style", hint "Choose how replies are written" |
| Another style | "Style · Concise" and × (back to Normal) | "Style: Concise. Change", and × "Remove style Concise" |

## The picker ("Use style")

- **Title** "Use style", and "How Aria writes its replies — not what it knows or does."
- Normal, Concise, Formal and Explanatory as a radio group, each with one line on what changes and a check on the chosen one. **Your styles** below, each tagged "From your writing".
- **The preview**: "Preview · Concise", the familiar request ("Summarize the October release.") and the same answer written in that style. It shows the chosen style; each other row has a small **Preview** button ("Preview Formal", a 44 / 48 target) that shows its preview without applying it. The pattern previews on hover or focus; a phone has neither, and tapping a row applies it.
- **Create & edit styles** at the foot opens the card below (the host's `onCreate`).
- Choosing applies the style at once and closes the picker. Nothing is sent.

## What happens

| Event | Result | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Choose a style | Chip names it; a line under the composer: "Concise applies to new messages, edits and retries — earlier replies keep their style." (without the second half when there are no replies yet) | "Style: Concise. Shorter, more direct replies. Your text is unchanged." |
| Back to Normal (× or choosing Normal) | Chip reads "Style"; "Back to Normal." with **Undo** | "Back to Normal. Your text is unchanged." |
| Undo | The style comes back | "Style: Concise." |
| Send | The style stays; the line goes | "Sent with the Concise style. It stays until you change it." |

Each reply carries the style it was written in: "Aria · Concise style".

## Create a style

A card in the conversation (the pattern's), not inside the composer.

1. **Source**: "Create a style", "Aria learns how you want replies to read — from writing you like, or from a description." **Start from**: An example / A description (a two-segment control). An example: "Paste writing you like" with "Used only to make this style." A description: "Describe the style". **Generate style** (the only AI step) is enabled once there are words; **Cancel**.
2. **Busy**: "Generating…" on the button with the working mark, and a progress line "Generating a style". The host generates and answers `generated` or `failed`. A late answer after Cancel or Back is ignored.
3. **Review**: "Style made by Aria from your example", then **Style name** (a field), **What it changes** (a field), **Instructions behind it** (a disclosure opening the instructions field), the preview of the new style (the host's, when it has one), then **Back**, **Save** and **Save and use**. Save needs a name and instructions.
4. **Failed**: "Aria couldn’t make a style from that. Try again, or start from a description instead." (or "…or describe it differently." from a description) with **Try again**.

Saving adds the style under Your styles ("Saved: Release notes voice. It’s in Your styles."); Save and use also chooses it.

## What the host supplies

The styles (`{ id, name, description, mine?, instructions? }`; `DEFAULT_STYLES` is the pattern's four), the previews (`{ question, answers }`; `DEFAULT_STYLE_PREVIEWS`), whether the conversation has replies yet, the current style (controlled), and for creating: the generation itself and where saved styles are kept. The host sends the style (and a custom style's instructions) with the request as a setting.

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | As Modes' rows without icons; the "From your writing" tag 11 semibold on `muted`, led by the generated mark 11; Preview a 32 eye icon button in a 44 / 48 target |
| Preview | `muted`, radius 10: head 11 semibold `mutedForeground`, the request 12 `mutedForeground` italic, the answer 13 `foreground` |
| Section head | "Your styles", 11 semibold `mutedForeground` |
| Card | The kit's card: border, radius 16, padding 16; title 16 semibold; fields as the describe field in Voice & Tone; the segmented control two equal buttons in a `muted` track, the chosen one `background` |

## Accessibility

- The picker is a radio group; each option says what it changes, and a style of their own says so. Preview buttons have their own names and never apply anything.
- Every change is announced politely and says the text is unchanged; Undo is a real button beside the line it undoes.
- The card's steps are announced: generating, ready ("Style ready: Release notes voice. Review it, then save."), failed, saved. The fields have labels; the instructions disclosure says whether it is open.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **A Preview button on each row** (no hover or focus preview on a phone); the preview sits under the list, not beside it.
- **"From your writing" and "Style made by Aria" carry the generated mark** (`badge-info`), as the pattern asks, since 22 Oct when generated content got its own glyph.
- **The failure state** and its wording (the pattern draws only success).
- **The id for a saved style**, from its name.
- **Icon:** `pen-line` (Lucide's nearest to the pattern's Material `edit_note`).

## Not in scope (later)

- Uploading a file as the example (the host can fill the example field from one).
- Editing or deleting a saved style (Create & edit opens the card for a new one).

components.specText:
# Suggestions (additions)

The pattern library's **Suggestions** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `suggestions`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). Called **additions** in the kit, because the composer's `suggestions` option is already Suggested Prompts.

**The agent suggests a few details to add to the request someone is writing**, marked as its suggestion, added only if they choose, and never sent for them. Suggested Prompts help someone start; this improves a request already in progress. **Their words are never replaced.**

It is for a request that is missing a detail the product can reliably infer from context (a time range, an audience, a constraint). It isn't offered while someone is still typing, and it never proposes a different request.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/additions.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/additions.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## The composer option

`additions: { suggest(text) → { items, why? } | null }` on the one `PromptComposer`. The host decides what fits the text so far; the kit decides when to ask and how it looks.

- **When**: after the text has been still for 900 ms, once per request, and only when the field isn't empty. Never on a keystroke.
- **Withdraws** quietly when the request changes so the offer no longer fits (the host's `suggest` returns nothing for the new text).
- **At most three** items.

## The row

Just above the composer, outside it:

- A top line with "Aria suggests" (words only, no glyph, as in Voice & Tone), **Why** and **Dismiss**; under it the items as chips with `plus`, wrapping onto new lines so each reads in full (a phone has no room for them beside the tag): "Include unresolved blockers", "Group the work by owner", "Compare with the August release". Each is read "Add to prompt: Include unresolved blockers".
- **Why** (`info`, "Why these suggestions", expanded or collapsed) opens one line: "Release summaries are read to decide what still needs attention — 3 blockers are open." Shown only when the host gives a reason.
- **Dismiss** (`x`, "Dismiss suggestions").
- The group is named "Suggestions from Aria". When it appears: "Suggestions from Aria: include unresolved blockers, group the work by owner, or compare with the August release."

## What happens

| Event | Result | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Add | The words go after the person's: "Summarize the September release." becomes "Summarize the September release and include unresolved blockers." (a question gains "Also include …"). The row becomes a line: "Added “and include unresolved blockers” to your request. You can edit it." with **Undo** | "Added to your prompt. Nothing was sent." |
| Edit after adding | The line goes; the words are theirs now | — |
| Undo (while the field is unchanged since adding) | The field goes back to their words; no more suggestions for this request | "Removed what was added. Your request is as you wrote it." |
| Dismiss | "Suggestions dismissed. They won’t come back for this request." until the next edit | "Suggestions dismissed." |
| The request no longer fits | The row goes, quietly; a later pause may offer again | — |
| Send | Everything resets for the next request | — |

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Row | Above the composer, 8 below anything above it; 1pt `border`, radius 16; the tag 12 semibold `mutedForeground` on a line with the two icon buttons |
| Chips | At least 32 tall in 44 / 48 targets, `background` with 1pt `border`, `plus` 14 and 13 medium `foreground`; they wrap, and a long one wraps its text |
| Why, Dismiss | Icon buttons, 44 / 48 |
| Why line | 12 `mutedForeground`, under the chips |
| Lines | As the composer's setting notes: 12 `mutedForeground`, with Undo a text button |

## Accessibility

- The row is a named group; each chip says what it adds; Why says whether it is open.
- The row is announced once when it appears, and every change is announced politely; focus stays in the field.
- Undo is a real button beside the line it undoes.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **The name "additions"** in the kit.
- **Undo only while the field is unchanged** since adding (the pattern restores the earlier text whatever happened since; that could lose their edits).
- **Appending**: "and …" after a statement, "Also …" after a question or exclamation, the suggestion alone in an empty field; a first word in capitals ("SSO") keeps its case.
- **No AI glyph** on "Aria suggests" until the library's one-glyph-per-meaning update lands.
- The wording of the offer, Undo and dismissal announcements.

components.specText:
# Prompt Enhancer

The pattern library's **Prompt Enhancer** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `prompt-enhancer`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). **Proposes a clearer version of the request someone wrote**, with every addition marked and explained, and the original kept until they choose.

It is a reviewable suggestion, never a silent rewrite: rewrites that replace a prompt with longer AI text hide what changed and can shift the intent. It is for a short or vague request the product can make more specific without guessing; not for requests that are already specific, and not to make every prompt longer.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/enhancer.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/prompt-enhancer.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

## The composer option

`enhance: { improve(text) → Promise<changes> }` on the one `PromptComposer`. The host proposes **additions**, each `{ id, add, why, assumption? }`, appended after the original in order (" from the last 30 days", ", grouped by onboarding step"). The kit never replaces words.

- **Improve prompt** is the last row of the composer's tune control (`specs/modes.md`, Request settings), with the AI action mark; while it works the row reads "Improving…" and choosing it stops. (Before 21 Oct it sat in the composer's controls: the kit's AI action (`AiActionButton`, icon only on a phone: "Improve with Aria"), so it carries the reserved glyph as every AI action does.) It needs words.
- **While improving**: the kit's working line above the composer, "Improving your prompt…", with **Stop**. The original stays in the field, untouched and editable; editing it drops the pending answer quietly.

## The review card

Above the composer, a region named "Suggested improvements to your prompt". It takes its natural height up to 60% of the window and scrolls inside beyond that (with the keyboard up the card can be taller than the room):

- **Suggested improvements**, and "2 of 3 changes".
- **You wrote**: the original. **Improved**: the original with each addition underlined and numbered (never colour alone); a change left out is struck through. Read aloud: "Improved: Analyze onboarding feedback, added 1: from the last 30 days, added 2: grouped by onboarding step, removed 3: propose three experiments."
- **The changes**, one row each with a checkbox (ticked = kept): "Add “from the last 30 days”", the reason, and the assumption as a tag ("Assumes the last 30 days."). Read "Change 1: Add “from the last 30 days”. Keeps it to the feedback since the new flow shipped. Assumes the last 30 days."
- **Keep original** and **Use improved** (unavailable when every change is left out).

## What happens

| Event | Result | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Improve | The working line with Stop; the field is unchanged | "Improving your prompt. Your original stays in the composer." |
| Answer | The card | "Suggested improvements ready: 3 changes. Your original is still in the composer." |
| Nothing to add | A line: "Nothing to add. This request is already specific." | the same |
| Failure | A line: "Couldn’t improve this request. Your original is unchanged." with **Try again** | the same |
| Untick / tick | Struck through / underlined again | "Left out: propose three experiments." / "Put back: …" |
| Use improved | The field holds the improved request; a line "Prompt updated. Nothing was sent." with **Undo** | "Prompt updated. Nothing was sent." |
| Undo (while the field is unchanged since) | The original comes back | "Back to your original." |
| Keep original | The card goes | "Kept your original." |
| Stop | The wait ends; a late answer is dropped | "Stopped improving. Your original is unchanged." |
| Edit the field | A pending answer or the card for the old words goes; after Use, Undo goes | — |

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Card | The kit's card above the composer: 1pt `border`, radius 16, padding 12; title 15 semibold; count 12 `mutedForeground` |
| Before and after | Stacked on a phone (the pattern sets them side by side): heads 11 semibold `mutedForeground`; text 14 `foreground`; additions underlined with a superscript-style number (11 semibold), left out struck through in `mutedForeground` |
| Rows | Checkbox in a 44 / 48 target; label 14 medium; reason 13 `mutedForeground`; the assumption a tag 11 semibold on `muted` with `info` |
| Lines | As the composer's setting notes, with Undo or Try again a text button |

## Accessibility

- The card is a named region; the improved text has a spoken form that says what was added and removed; each change is a checkbox that says what it adds, why, and what it assumes.
- Every step is announced politely; the field keeps focus and the original until Use.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **Before and after stacked**, not side by side (a phone's width).
- **Undo only while the field is unchanged** since Use, as in Suggestions.
- **Nothing to add** as its own outcome (the pattern draws success and failure only).
- **No Edit button**: Use puts the improved request in the field, where it is already editable.
- The spoken forms and announcements.

components.specText:
# Madlibs

The pattern library's **Madlibs** pattern (branch-2, the Prompt Scaffolds group added 19 Oct 2026: `material-patterns.js` → `madlibs`; the Planboard simulator in `material-sim.js`). **A request written as a sentence with a few labelled blanks**: fill them, read the result, then edit it in the composer before sending.

The hard part of many requests is remembering which details matter. A sentence with blanks asks for exactly those, while the person still sees and owns the words that will be sent. It is for common requests with two to four variable details (summaries, briefs, comparisons); more than four is a form (Structured Input), not a sentence.

The rules and wording live in `react-native/src/madlibs.ts`. `npm run fixtures` writes `specs/madlibs.fixtures.json`, and SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter are tested against it.

**Madlibs and Templates.** The library renamed the fill-in-the-blank sentence (our Templates, `specs/templates.md`) to Madlibs and changed its rules: blanks are typed or picked, there are optional clauses and suggested values, and it never sends. Templates now means a reusable workflow setup (revision backlog item 5). Madlibs is a new component; the existing Templates stays until it is rebuilt as the new Templates.

## The sentence

`"Create a summary of {project} for {audience}[, focusing on {topic}]."` with each blank `{ id, label, required, suggestions }`. Text in `[ ]` is an **optional clause**: it leaves the sentence with its blank when that is empty. Each blank appears once; at most four (`madlibFits`).

## The card

A card in the conversation, a group named "Guided prompt":

- **Build your request**.
- **The sentence, live**: the words with each blank shown in place: its value, or its label while empty (muted, underlined, never passed off as a value). An optional clause is muted while its blank is empty. **Preview** under it: the request exactly as it will be placed ("Create a summary of Checkout redesign for …." while a required blank is empty).
- **The fields**, one per blank in sentence order: the label ("Project", "Topic · optional"), a text field (placeholder: the label in lower case), and its suggestions as chips that fill it. Read "Project, required". A value the agent inferred is italic with a **Suggested** tag and **Keep**, until kept or changed; any filled field has a clear button.
- **Nothing is sent until you send it.** and **Use prompt** ("Replace your message" when the composer holds words the person wrote).
- **After Use**: the card becomes "Placed in the composer — edit it there", and the composer holds the request, editable and unsent.

## What happens

| Event | Result | Announced |
|---|---|---|
| Type | The value and the preview change | — |
| Pick a suggestion | The field fills | "Audience: leadership." |
| The agent suggests | An empty blank fills, marked Suggested | "Suggested project: Checkout redesign. Keep it or change it." |
| Keep / change | The mark goes | "Kept: Checkout redesign." |
| Clear | The blank empties (an optional clause leaves) | "Topic cleared." |
| Use, a required blank empty | Nothing moves; the empty required fields are outlined with "Add project — required." and the card says "Add project and audience — required. Everything else is kept." | the same |
| Use | The request goes into the composer | "Placed in the composer. Edit it, then send." |

## Look

| | |
|---|---|
| Card | The kit's card: 1pt `border`, radius 16, padding 12 |
| Sentence | 15 `foreground`; a blank's value semibold; an empty blank its label in `mutedForeground`, underlined dotted; a suggested value italic |
| Fields | As the describe field in Voice & Tone (44 / 48 tall); label 13 semibold, "optional" 12 `mutedForeground`; a missing one outlined in `destructive` with the words under it; the Suggested tag 11 semibold on `muted` |
| Suggestion chips | As Suggestions' chips, 32 tall in 44 / 48 targets |

## Accessibility

- Each field is labelled with its blank, whether it is required, and a suggested value; the preview is read as text.
- Validation names the missing blanks in words, not colour alone, and keeps everything entered.
- Every change is announced politely; Use moves nothing but the text.

## Ours, not the pattern's

- **Fields under the sentence** rather than inside it (inline fields wrap poorly on a phone); the sentence above shows each value in place.
- **Replace your message** when the composer holds the person's own words (as Templates did).
- **Keep** as a button beside the Suggested tag (the pattern keeps a suggestion when it is changed).
- The announcements.

it('the chip names the base and its count, with a 44 / 48 target', async () => {
